I also like how the progression affects the way the base looks, adding high tech gadgets to backgrounds and characters.
While I wasn't a fan of the art direction of the game, sprites are well drawn and design are interesting, music is quite decent too, especially night tracks, adding even more atmosphere to already tense night missions, probably for the first time done right since UFO Defense / TFTD. Different UFOs, alien bases and terror missions, destroyable environments, most things X-Com fan loves is here.
Not everything is perfect, though. Research tree feels too linear, economy and base management are lacking because there's no need to buy/manufacture new aircraft weapons and conventional equipment for troops, everything is given for free or upgrades automatically. Alien research giving 10% bonus to damage for some reason also reeks of XCOM. Manufacturing was also completely killed, with products selling for only half a price on the market, after your engineer wasting unique materials and time on production. While I understand that it was made to fix the "OPness" manufacturing had in original games, but not only it makes no sense, it also makes manufacturing a waste of money once you unlock next tier of equipment and previous gear becomes more or less obsolete. Since both labs/engineering and living quarters require a lot of space and support only 15 people, unlike ~50 in original game + more space for building in bases, the game could still be balanced if there was at least some profit in manufacture. Battlescape also has its share of problems, with some badly designed choke points in small UFOs, UFO assault being a game of peek-a-boo with aliens by using door controls, some maps that repeat over and over again, enemies psi-attacking your troops even without having a line of sight on them, and very bad ballistics that remind me more of terrible RNG XCOM combat, and occasional shenanigans like bullet from sniper on third floor being blocked by car parked in the line on sight half way to the target on ground level. 20 years after release of original X-Com no game (aside from Silent Storm) can still replicate its proper ballistics, and it's a damn shame. And the lack of 3D geoscape is a shame too, but nothing you can do about it, engine is fully 2D, and project lead already said that this engine was a bad idea to begin with.
But all in all, Xenonauts is the first game I could actually call a proper remake to X-Com. If you love X-Com and didn't like the simplicity of XCOM, then definitely give Xenonauts a go.

The true spiritual successor to the fabled original  UFO: Enemy Unknown from 1994
While the recent 3D XCOM: Enemy Unknown by Firaxis was a decent game in itself and has some great ideas it was very limited (Or "streamlined"), especially in terms of the strategic side of the game where things like base building and base missions were markedly absent (And the scripted one from Enemy Within doesn't count :p ).
This game has it all, I cannot see a feature missing from the original game that is not implemented in this one. Think the 1994 version lovingly re-implemented with modern tech and a fun little UFO interception mini-game.
There is also some great writing in the research reports etc. which give character to otherwise static screens.
Downsides? The graphics are not great (But then you do not care about that do you?) and the tactical map selection can be limited. There is a solution to the second issue in that this game is moddable and there are already map-pack mods out there to increase selection.
Im summary: The main thing is... I actually feel like the boss of an organisation dedicated to protecting humanity from the Aliens and making tough decisions rather than a spare tyre like in the recent remake.
Massive thumbs up.

First, I only installed this game via Steam to write a review about it. I played well over 800hrs in the non-steam version over the past 8 years. I was one of the people voting for Steam's green light.  Thus I cannot comment on the steam free to play versin with only two classes available.
In my opinion, many negative reviews I read were putting the game into the wrong drawer, so I wanted to explain the scale and possibilities it has over others.
- yes, the graphics are compared to anything newer than 2001 shocking
- yes, the UI befits the graphics and needs a lot of good will to getting used to.
- yes, you do not know what to do once you logged in.
- no, it is not a CoD-ish first person shooter.
I played many games like World of tanks, planes, ships, etc after I played sudden strike, blitzkrieg, CoD, Red Orchestra and panzer general in my early days. I always hoped for a game combining all elements of an army (Land, Air, Sea) in first person on the very same map and a large map at best.
At one day, I found WW2OL. It topped my wildest dreams. Not only did it combine all elements, but the map was whole western europe and it was a war, going on without me being online, but also without me losing any property while not there.
Let me give you some examples:
- Additional to infantry, you can play as fighter pilot, bomber pilot, the one using the bombsight, tank driver, commander, gunner, anti-tank-gunner, flak-gunner, commanding a patrol boat, destroyer, stuka, etc.
- all these roles play together on the same map, attack together the same target or support each other.
- you could sneak as infantry close to a town and observe with your binoculars the defences, marking enemy guns or tanks or soldiers.
- a nearby bomber sees the markings or reads the callouts and begins to circle the area to find the enemy and take him out.
- this game has no minimap with automatic display of enemies. Only marked enemies by you or other players are visible on the map. This of course means, that an enemy infantry or tank could from the time of your marking til the time your bomber sees the mark be well away of your originaly pinpointed location.
- while you fight a town, some players decide to cut supply for the defenders by blowing up a bridge 1km away with explosives, while other players fly a bombing run against another bridge far to the east.
- others boarded a transport plane and prepare for a parachute jump over town.
- some players driving tanks settled on a hill nearby town, while other guard them against sappers as infantry and others drive ammo to them.
- other players spawned in fighter planes to clear the air of enemy fighters and make it safe for the bomber pilots.
- you see 2 ducked enemy infantry rushing through some bushes. Do you shoot at them, or do you let them pass by and search sneakily from where they came? maybe they have a mobile spawn, from where more of them could come. If you could find it and take it out, you might well have influenced the outcome.
- towns/villages have districts. These are marked by a building with a flag. these are the focus of the fights. You have to capture such a building with a timer, to capture that district and possibly aswell an enemy spawnpoint like a depot, from where he spawns infantry, anti-air/tank guns or even large army bases, from where he spawns tanks to defend the town.
These were only some examples of possibilities you could meet. I saw it all. From a para jump with well over 30 players, while flak shells exploded around us and machine guns shot at us from down below, to house fights in towns and villages to long dogfights high above etc or ruse attacks on one village to attack short after the real target. It has a nice layer of tactical decisions, usualy the average joe doesnt see, as others take care of it.
This game is so much more than just 10 tanks vs. 10 tanks or 10 planes vs. 10 planes. Do try to lift off one before you judge the complexity of this game. Never had I a better feeling in a ww2 game, than when a friendly plane bombs the bunkers in front of me and I can advance as inf deeper into the town.
Everything is player driven. Even the high command (the ones calling targets to attack and defend) are players.
A campaign doesnt last hours. it lasts days to weeks!
The sound is actualy quiet superb imo. You can hear the direction of it, including footsteps, can judge the gun and with that even if its an enemy or friend you hear.
No other game managed to combine all this on one battlefield even a 100th as large as this and on that level of "realism", difficulty and immersion.
I supported green light out of a simple reason. All this features and possibilities are awesome. But only epic, when many people play it. The comunity is certainly one of the finest out there, but kept ofc dwindeling over the years. I wished the developers and the comunity an influx of many new players, since this game was even for me very hard to find, as it has basicaly 0 press.
It all feels a bit odd and ugly and old and indeed has a steep learning curve.
If you like such content, give it a try. If you can't get past the clunkienes and graphics, no problem. A foot soldier is indeed all you need to give it a sniff.

For many years, SEGA and Nintendo were at each other's throats. Many children from the 90's sided with their favorite mascots: Sonic the Hedgehog or Mario the Plumber. When Mario made his jump to 3D in '96, in "Super Mario 64", critics and fans were blown away at his debut into the next generation, while many waited patiently for Sonic to make his debut, until... well.... this sh** came out.
I'm going to be totally honest. Sonic Adventure is a bad game. I know that there is a strong community behind Sonic, but remember this dear reader: I am playing this not because I'm looking for a good Sonic game or just shamelessly trying to promote Mario. I'm playing this because I love good video games and I want to play as many as possible. And Sonic Adventure just isn't a good game.
Sonic Adventure follows Sonic and Tails on their quest to stop Dr. Eggman (for the fourth time) as well as also focusing on the stories of Knuckles collecting the Master Emerald's shattered pieces, Amy trying to protect her birdy, E-102 Gamma learning about his inner humanity, and Big the Cat... catching his frog-friend...
Yeah, my biggest complaint is that the story sucks. And it's not just the actual plot (and plots specifically that focus on these characters)- it's the way that terrible plot is executed. The anaimation and lip-syncing is terrible. Every cutscene has something wrong in it- whether it be the terrible voice acting, awkward animation, inconsistent information in and out of frame (E.g. in one shot, Sonic is sitting and staring at Eggman, and in the next he's standing up and staring at Eggman). Not only that, but the dialogue is re-written in each scene with the new characters you play as, so there isn't even a strong continuity between the playable characters. And the dialogue itself is cheesy and very cringe-worthy. I'd honestly call this game "So bad it's good", if it weren't for the gameplay. In fact let's talk about the gameplay for each character.
SONIC: Pretty decent. He occasionally controls well, but a lot of his levels have bottomless pits that are easy to slip into if you have too much velocity. That and the camera is very awkward.
TAILS: Not really my cup of tea. For some reason, you have to race and beat Sonic to the end of the stage. I'm more curious as to why Tails is even doing this if it wasn't established earlier. The levels are the same as Sonic with a lot of the beginning trimmed off and some flying rings thrown in to increase your speed. A bit lazy when it comes to making new levels.
KNUCKLES: Probably my favorite character. He's a little fast and the chaos emeralds are sometimes hidden the dumbest places but Knuckles plays so well that I don't really care.
AMY: Terrible. She's too slow and clunky to actually be any fun. That and her voice actress is definitely the most atrocious.
BIG: Surprisingly decent, despite the outrageous decision. Who thinks about fishing while playing a Sonic game? The fishing, while the frog can be stubborn, is actually somewhat enjorable... despite how short-lived it is. I just hate how pontless Big's story is in the grand scheme of things. It feels like a waste of time.
E-102 GAMMA: Kind of boring. His stages are over far too quickly (Including bosses), and his motivations are very vague and confusing. It's by far the easiest story-mode in the game.
I think that while this is a very ambitious title for its time, its poor execution left what was going to be the shining launch title for the Dreamcast... into the eventual failure that we are familiar with today. I was either bored, frustrated, or laughing my a** off with how poorly the game was put together. If you want the full experience of Sonic Adventure, here's my suggestion- find the Game Grumps playthrough of the game and get stoned like a mother f***er. That's the only way I can imagine you'd find pleasure in playing this horribly buggy and irritating game. I'm giving Sonic Adventure a 2/10. Don't waste your time or money on this lousy port. You've got so much else to live for and enjoy,

Tomb Raider: Legend is the first game in the first reboot of the franchise, created by Crystal Dynamics after they took over the franchise from Core Design.
TR:L story start off with a flashback when Lara was just a young girl, when she was travelling on a plane with her mother, which suddenly crashes and leave them as the only survivors. Lara and her mother finds an ancient site where they, by accident, activates it, which results in her mother suddenly disappearing through a portal. Years later, Lara is a renown explorer and archelogist on her way to find a similar site in order to uncover what truly happened to her mother. Obviously that wont be easy and she immidiately stumbles into others who wishes to use these sites as well.
The gameplay is pretty much what is typical for the classical Tomb Raider game; you arrive at some place and do puzzles to progress further into the levels, some places have secrets which requires you to do something special in order to get the Relics and artifacts. Controls are pretty much standard in the series, where you use the movement keys to move around, space to jump and some additional keys to do special things such as grapple.
Most of the combat comes in the form of facing literal hordes of humans coming at you, and while the numbers might scare you, they're pretty stupid, at least on the easier difficulties. The game can automatically aim for you, so you don't really have to aim yourself like in most other games.
As something new in the series, the game actually gives you the chance to ride with Lara's motorcycle! However, it is pretty straightforward rather than open for you to explore while riding it, and it happens only in, imo, the most boring levels in the game where you do nothing for 5 minutes than drive on the motorcycle and shoot hordes of enemies.
The graphics are rather decent considering it came out in 2006. I played the game  way back in either 2007 ot 2008 and while I didnt have the best PC back then, I experienced some of the same graphical issues that I had back then, raging from crazy textures glitching like hell, lightning/shadows going bonkers and last but not least, textures that appear transparent yet still have *some* textures, so at some points it was hard to see where to go, especially during the level where you ride a motorcycle.
I have some faint memories of when the game was announced and how scared I was what would happen to the Lara we all loved from the classical franchise. I also remembered the games gained a lot of criticism, that I agree on, that the games began to lose its focus on Lara's adventures as an archeologist and became more of a "I need to murder my way to get where I want" kind of a thing. My impression was that Crystal Dynamics wanted to reboot the franchise to give the game a bit of a better outlook and make the game refreshing and new, however, within the first minute into the game you literally murder one of the mercenaries for no proper reason. Even the supporting characters, which I have to admit were horribly annoying during the game with their bad jokes, puns and constant comments on literally *EVERYTHING* in the game, asked why the guy was there, whereas Lara more or less answers "lol idk". I mean, I could justify the murder if it was in self-defence, but oh well.
Overall, I still think the game is enjoyable, albeit it is incredibly short and many of the puzzles are very very easy to go through, at least if you ignore most of the secrets. If you can play through the game without having any bugs or glitches with the gameplay, graphics and cutscenes, then I am sure most people would enjoy this game.
PROS
+ is in the spirit of the classical games
+ controls are easy to get into
+ story is not the best, but it keeps you interested
+ the sword ;)
CONS
- way too short (game can be finished in around 5-6 hours)
- puzzles are too easy and offers too little challenge
- doesn't really fix the "problem(s)" of the previous games regarding the enemies
- those damned motorcycle levels....

The camera angles are the worst offender of the game, and ruin the entire experience. The controls might have actually worked alright as well if it weren't for the heavy reliance on the camera to be exactly where it needs to be at any given time. As it turned out, this issue plagued the overall gameplay even further when jumping from one place to another.
I could speak to many other problems I came across, but none of them come close to the ones I've mentioned above. The game is lightyears better than Angel of Darkness, but there aren't many games out there that aren't. So, in summation, this is not the return to form I had hoped it would be, and while I will probably stick it out to the end (as I've also heard it's rather short), it does not make me look forward to playing the next two entries.

I've never played a game quite like Labyrinthine Dreams, a very human and realistic story set in a very surreal and atmospheric dream. Labyrinthine Dreams tells the tale of Beth, a young woman struggling to find her place in the world while dealing with her ever-present anxieties. Beth comes face to face with a serious illness which forces her to look deep within and find what is truly meaningful in life.
The gameplay revolves around a series of puzzles, each unique and challenging and brought to life with lush mapping, atmospheric effects, and a dazzling soundtrack. These puzzles are difficult, but figuring them out is immensly satisfying and their ever changing nature always keeps you on your toes.
The most impressive thing about this game is the seamless cohesion between the puzzles and Beth's story. Each puzzle has a discernable symbolic relationship with a critical period in Beth's life and her battles with her inner demon are among the games finest moments.
This is an extremely unique game which is definitely worth a purchase. It isn't very long but the journey is well worth an hour or two of your day. While the player learns the specifics of Beth's illness, but her story is universal and can be appreciated by anybody dealing with any sort of oppresive force in their life. Give this game a shot, you won't be disappointed.

Eversion might not be the most beautiful game or even the most innovative one , but it's still a very nice experience. The whole gameplay relies on a layers gimmick. You switch between them to navigate through obstacles, collect the diamonds and reach the goal. The further the layer, the weirder the surroundings and the harder the challenge.
Although the gameplay is very fun, it's the mood that is set by each of the layers that really captures one's attention. You go from a poppy bright cheerful world into a twisted dark one. What should be pointed out is that the music plays a big role in maintaining the right feel for each of the dimensions. When it comes to the ending (well all 3 of them), it's the cherry on top of the cake.
All in all, I recommend this game to everyone who likes platformers, indie games or puzzle games but remember to keep in mind that the game lasts only for about 2 hours before you have everything unlocked. It's quite a shame because Eversion has potential to be much better than it already is.

2D side scrolling platformer. You jump on enemies, collect gems and try to reach a flag at the end of each level. The hero doesn't have any special powers, and there's no power-ups to be collected either. The world is colorful, bright and playfully decorated. Sounds like a real drag, eh?
Now here's the twist: by visiting certain places in each level, you make the world everse into darker and more hellish dimensions so that you can reach that famous flag at the end. Enemies gets quicker and more sinister, devil hands try to reach out from the pits to grab you, the colors shift to desolate, icy, bleak and the bushes and flowers wither and die. Oh, and there's a fog from hell chasing you, wanting to consume all in it's path.
What makes the game great is the aestethic, and the replay value added in the achievements. It's a pretty short game, but as a piece of art it's well worth it's money. I'd buy it again.
8/10, as far as artsy, weird platformers go.

Ah Tomb Raider Legend, the first game developed by Crystal Dynamics, creators of the famous Legacy of Kain series (e.g. Soul Reaver). I remember I was not concerned that different people would continue the series because I played those games and really enjoyed them. The story involves Lara's mother, Avalon, and the famous King Arthur's sword - excalibur. CDynamics promised that Lara will go back to what she does best - raiding tombs and they kept the word. Game mechanics are easy to learn and the overall game is a lot of fun (there are 3 levels where you ride a motorbike)! What's important to mention is the Croft Manor returns where you can practice movements and uncover few secrets. The graphics are very nice, music is very good just like in every Tomb Raider. I think every fan of the classics was satisfied with what we received. Finally is time to write few words about Lara as she is essential to the series. In my opinion she is great, she's still acrobatic and tough and still beautiful (her original creator was brought back to help). Miss Croft has new voice which I personally like it a lot and think it fits her character perfectly. New developers surely did a great job bringing back Lara from her downfall so that we could once again feel the thrill of her adventures.

Hands down my favorite TR. Super refreshing from the older games. A bit heavy on the cinematics and I wish there was more gameplay overall, but this game was totally thrilling and I loved the different settings throughout. Also Lara's character is awesome in this game (not so much in Underworld...)
A+!

Tomb Raider: Legend was one of the first TR games I played and therefore has significant nostalgic value in my book.
1. The storyline is quite short, it takes about 5.5 hours to get through the game on medium difficulty. I'd rate the story itself a 6/10. Visiting a few tombs for sword pieces to kill a monster isn't the strongest storyline I've seen in a game, but overall fun to follow along.
2. Graphics are fine for a 10 year-old game, nothing extraordinary for 2006 but not bad either.
3. The game has a few bugs where you'd get stuck in between movable objects or invisible walls, not game-breaking at all but they are there. You can always re-load the previous checkpoint to get unstuck if you can't manage it by wiggling yourself free.
4. I'd say it is an enjoyable game which can be bought for just a few bucks during Steam Sale, a must have for any TR fan.

The Penny Arcade series reinvented in 16-bit era JRPG style. Basically the same combat system as Zeboyd's earlier games, crossed with Penny Arcade humor. The story is not great but not awful and it does tie back into the events established by the first two parts.  Other people have complained that it's linear, especially in the "overworld", and that is certainly true, but I'm not really bothered by it. For me, the biggest problem with PA3 is that PA4 is so much worse.  This game ends on a cliffhanger and finding out how the story ends requires you to play the sequel ... and unfortunately, it turns out that PA4 is somewhere between mediocre and terrible.  If you like a good old-school hack-and-slash RPG and aren't too hung up on understanding the things happening in the story, you could definitely play PA3 by itself and have a lot of fun.

This is bar far the best open world/MMORPG/moba I have ever played. Now "bear" with me on this one, because while an open world moba may seem strange at first, it is executed brilliantly here. As soon as I booted up the game I was greeted with the most beutiful cinimatic I have ever seen I my life, the sound of metal coliding and warriors crying out in rage and glorious victory, it truely captured the feelings of the next 26 hours I would spend with the game before writing this review. Now without spoiling anything, you play as a adventurer on the side of one of 6 fections fighting for control of the legendary castle of Alkenwol (witch lies at the center of the world map.). Now I personally chose the Aricaria Kingdom but started to regret my choice as I learned more about there political standpoint. Now im not sure why the devs were so heavy handed with the classist undertones, but it didnt take away from my overall enjoyment. So now onto what really struck me about the game, the graphics. My word, these are by far the best graphics ive seen in an MMO, or any game for that matter. After the tutorial you are given a wide view of the land ahead. You can already feel the adventures you are soon to have. What really suprised me was how well optomized this game was, at no point, even in some of the 1000 vs 1000 player battles did i every have my FPS drop lower than 57. The load times are a bit of a hastle sometimes but being such a large world it is to be expected. But I never found myself iritated by the load times considering you are able to change your loadout and spell slots while you wait. Now to get a good idea of what the graphics are like (because the screen shots are wildly inacurate) think The Witcher 3 meets MGS V, but even that doesnt do it justice. But we still havent tralked about charecter creation. Now each of the 6 factions have there own set of 4 races, but there are neutral races that can fight for any side, so there are are total of 27 races to chose from. and in terms of classes there are 6 faction specific classes and then there are 10 classes other than thoes. So now we have a whopping 27 races and 16 classes, but the customization doesnt end there, because you can mix and match the classes. When you pick your class you can chose any 2 you want from your options. Want to be a Tank that knows a few spells, then you just set the Berzerker class to primary and the Sorcerer class to secondary, and walla, now you are a Flame axe ravager. Of course there is a trade off and now you will be less armoured compared to the other berzerkers and you arent as magically skilled as the sorcerer but you have more tactical options. So there I was, set up as a Lvl 1 War blade Summoner (Standard warrior crossed with necromancer) and I was able to start my questing. Now the way the map is set up, you have 3 lanes set up for each faction, leading to the castle at the center, these lanes are lined with towns and quest spots, but for the real questing you will want to enter the wilderness between lanes. So the general gameplay loop involves, going to one of the many towns, begin tracking a quest, and once it is completed, usually by going into the "jungle" and slaying some kind of monster or helping some people out with a bandit problem, your faction gets a boost of some kind, sometimes its just dps agains the enemy factions, and other times its something less obviouse, like the shops along the lanes are more fully stocked and able to trade. But it all helps out your faction in reaching the Castle and wining the game. The combat itself it fantastic, fast paced combat with blocking, parrying, and dodging away from enemy attacks, it just makes the overall gameplay loop that much more enjoyable. The pvp is great and amazingly well balanced. But the real game takes place within your own lands. You see, each kingdom is ruled by an actual player, this ruler is able to command the NPC warriors of the kingdom and make laws for the land, but he can be replaced at any time if the people (thats you, the players) decied to turn against him. if he is killed, it becomes a vote on who should become the next ruler, the player who organized the raid against the old ruler starting with 50 votes since they did alot of work to change things in the faction. The King or Queen is'nt able to do everything however and is watched over by a moderator who ensures that they arent just sitting around not doing anything, if the ruler hasnt loged on for more than a 4 days to do a quick check up on how things are going, they are kicked off the throne and a new ruler, (chosen ahead of time by the old ruler) is put in place. Now im sure alot of this is seeming daunting to you, but trust me when i say, it makes for one of the most immersive, interactive and engaging gameplay expiriences you will every have. Eversion is not what you think. The unassuming and colorful visuals are intended not to delight, but to give you a false sense of security; to draw you in before transporting you to the nightmarish world of its reality. It's intentionally unsettling, and unique in how it manages to get under your skin while never assuming anything is wrong, which is what I find so remarkable about it.
The hook to Eversion is everting the world, similar to swapping dimensions, which causes the environment to change properties or even disappear. It's a simple mechanic that allows for some clever lever designs, but it is also where the game becomes very, very creepy. The deeper you go through the layers of everting, the more twisted the backgrounds become and the more deranged the music gets. The disclaimer at the start should tell you all you need to know: "this game is not suitable for children or those with a nervous demeanor."
Although it lacks the nuance of something like Braid, Eversion similarly uses video game cliches as the foundation of the experience, relying on your expectations to carry the premise as it warps the familiar into something all its own. In this developer Zaratustra Productions is mostly successful, with my only complaint being I wish there was more here. With the exception of a few odd secrets, you can complete and collect everything in around two hours (those disinclined to gather all the gems should expect half or less than that). Even with its low base price, it feels a little too much for what you get.
Aside from the price, Eversion is something I think is worth your time. It completely surprised me in its execution, leaving me chilled and a little disturbed, but impressed nonetheless. If you are looking for something off the beaten path, Eversion is one game that will absolutely deliver. It doesn't last long, but this strange journey is undoubtedly one worth taking, provided you are prepared for the potentially terrifying.

When this game was released in 2006, I bought it just because of the box art. I hadn't had any experience playing Tomb Raider before the purchase. The box and the information on it were simply too appealing to miss, combined with a positive review in the local games magazine. What I discovered after installation blew me away. Amazing locales, greatly variable and adaptive soundtrack (some tracks are among my all-time favourites) and first-class animation that I hadn't seen before in a game. It didn't matter much to me that the level design and puzzles were all too linear and quite easy because I was fully immersed in this first next-gen Lara Croft rendition and didn't realise at that time that I'm playing "just" a fancy acrobatics simulator. But the developers tried hard to capture the feeling of world exploration in a limited level space mainly by the incredible vistas. As for the gameplay, it's puzzle-heavy, with a terrible combat system (and some frustrating motorbike sections), but thankfully that doesn't take up much gameplay time. The boss fights are the most annoying thing about this game and they occur at the end of each level. Stylised collectables are a plus. Gold collectables are particularly difficult to obtain and will require you to tamper a bit with the puzzles. At the time of release, the game wasn't optimised well, especially the surprisingly ugly next-gen mode, that changes the feeling of the game completely, though for the worse turn. I recommend playing with it turned off. The controls and camera are a bit wonky, but you can get used to it. A bonus Croft Manor level is nice but otherwise, the game doesn't come with much replay value.

Just when you thought there would never be an episode 3, the gang is back in Precipice of Darkness. So it is review time.
Story- Some time has passed since the events of RSPoD 2 when Gabe and Tycho go on another mission to find out who Mr. Blood really is and what he is up to. But things are not what they seem to be as it seems everyone has a secret to hide. Just when you think you know someone. This story is quite darker than the previous two games with a fair amount of death, betrayals and lies. My main problem with the story, though, was where was my character from the first two games. After all he's  been through, he seems to dissapear from the game for good. Well, he (or she) is not forgotten as there is a little side game prolouge that explains his dissapearance, humorous but desturbing, that is all I will say on that. A-
Graphics- Well, Zeboyd games now takes the wheel for creating this game and so they took a completly different direction graphically. Remeber the old Final Fantasy games for the SNES? That is the style to expect for the remaining games. The retro style looks nice and well defined but may not be for everyone. C
Sound- There is no voice acting this time around and the retro sound effects are lifted straght from FF6 but the music is actually an improvement from the previous 2 games with a surprizingly rich score. B
Gameplay- This game plays just like an FF game from SNES days and that is not a bad thing. The controls are easy to get used to and are even better with controller options available (XBOX controller preferred). The dungeons are fun to explore and the battles are a blast from the past. There is even a class system for additional strategy in battle though the fights are relativly easy, it's fun to expirament with different combinations of classes. The down side is that the world map is very restrictive as you follow a strict path from point to point, making the game seem kinda restrictive. B+
Overall- Due to the poor sales of the first two games, the project was almost canceled, but was picked up by a different company to finish. As such, you cannot transfer saved games. Though they manage to find creative ways around this issue, it still feels dissapointing that you cannot continue as your created character and that really bugged me throughout. But it still was a fun game and much improved from its predecessors. Recommended. B-

This game was an enjoyable throwback to 16bit turn based RPGs, but with a twist. They improved the combat system by adding some complexity without making it overly complicated. Since the core of all these turned based RPGs is mostly how well and fulfilling the combat is, the majority of this review will go over that section in detail to give you a greater understanding of how the game plays. I broke down the review in bold sections so you can read what is most important or what is most interesting to you in order of importance.
At the end of this page there will be a Pro's Con's and overview which would be the closest thing I have to a "TLDR"
THE GUI (Graphic User Interface)
When you get into a battle in this game, you will see a very familar layout, the graphic user interface or (GUI) will probably remind you of a plethora of similar older turn based titles like the final fantasy series, chrono trigger, or the breathe  of fire series. You'll see fight or attack, item and Defend. However this is where the similarities end and some of the polishing of these older combat system begins. The menus themselves are fairly easy to navigate and use, nothing new to see here but nothing bad either.
The GUI also has one new feature which is really nice, which is a bar on the top of the screen with the portraits of each of your characters and the enemies on a visible time line which shows you who or what enemy is likely to be next in turn. I say likely because in this game there is a "speed" stat and interrupt mechanic attribute which can be manipulated to increase or decrease the likelihood of who's next to perform an action. Speed is exactly as it sounds, a flat given rate at how quickly your next turn comes. Once their portrait goes from the right side of the screen to the end of the bar on the left they start somewhere back on the right, distance moved on the bar per action or round spent is based on your speed stat.
Hovwering over an enemy unit will tell you the current hp of the unit, and how many elemental weaknesses it has, but not which ones. Its your job to explore and find them your self! It will also usually include some kind of humorous description of the unit, generally relevant or commenting on its aesthetics.
Other cool features are the skin changes, at any time outside of battle you may change your skin from "furry" "gender swapped" "undead" or "normal". I remember one battle actually had a condition of increasing the power of all female characters during it, but it wasn't an issue and this feature really is just there for your visual enjoyment.
One more thing of important note: This game has a range of 4 preset difficulties which can be changed at any time (outside of combat/dialogue), should the game not be challenging you enough or too much. It defaults on normal.
THE INTERRUPT FEATURE
You can slow targets, stop them, or increase your own speed, but the best feature is the interrupt feature. The interrupt feature allows you  to push back the time it takes of a current foes next turn. When you use an ability that has this feature you will see their portrait be pushed back. This effect generally is on a diminishing return so you can't "lock down" an opponent from ever being able to preform an action, but you certainly can hinder it, and many interrupt abilities later still deal damage, or have other bonuses like not costing MP! Usually every 2nd interrupt wont hit as hard as the previous. So interrupt 1 will give you a good knock back, 2 maybe not so much, but 3 will be powerful again and the pattern continues.
CUSTOMIZING YOUR CHARACTERS
This game has the traditional armor, weapon and accessorie slot, but the real customization begins with class pins.
Each character has its own unique abilities, and later on you get up to 14 (1 from an optional boss) "pins" which provide new abilities, passive abilities, and bonus to certain stats and pretty much work much like Espers or Materia for you final fantasy fans.
There are no restrictions on what character can wear what pin, so you can have quite a few different combinations. The equipped pins gain experience along with the character's core abilities as well, and unlike other older games the unequipped pins will still gain experience but not as quickly as the ones being used. However, each character will inevitably be able to wear 2 pins, so that only leaves 5 pins not at use at any given point in time.  So this lets you balance and combined 3 classes abilities on one character, his own, and the two pins you equip on to them. So any character can fit the role you decide to give to it.
OTHER IMPORTANT COMBAT MECHANICS
The most important feature in the combat here is that, you  can drag out a boss or any battle until you win but.... it gets much harder.. Ever so often the power of the NPCS get stronger, the longer the battle goes the more damage the abilties and attacks of the NPC's do. So only using one character to deal damage, while healing all the incoming damage is rarely an effective strategy. When you hover an enemy unit you'll see something like XXX% power, every interval they gain 10% more power. The longer you go... well... they start to hit harder and hurt more...
Certain battles even have conditions where certain types of damage or stats are increased (which affects everyone in most cases, you and your enemy). Most of the time these bonuses can be used in your advantage. Other times they add in a new element to the fight to over come and conquer.
MAGIC POINTS AND NON EQUIPMENT ITEMS REVISITED AND REDONE
Essentially every turn you get 1 MP or Magic point and you get a variety of abilities to use, but like any ability it has a cost, some are free, some have greater effect on the first turn, others cost more, and/or have other conditions or bonus effects. However there are items and abilites later in the game that allow you to gain MP faster, such as stealing it from your other allies, or energite, an item that can only be used so many times per battle thatr grants X MP.
Now to items, Items in this game are consumables that you can upgrade and have a limited number of charges per battle. Every battle they reset to full.
There are 6 different items to use in the game and they can be upgraded in two different ways, their effect (how powerful) and charges (how many uses).
OVERIEW: 8/10
PROS AND CONS
The tone of this review may sound to some overtly positive but this game isn't without its flaws so we will start with Con's first. There aren't too many though I am happy to say.
CONS:
Certain abilities or ability combos can become overwhelmingly powerful which cause you to stop using previous abilities or fall into routines.
The game is rather linear, and besides 2 optional bosses, and the Arena, there is little room to "Grind" or gain additional experience or $$$ to farm items, upgrades, and accessories.
The plot line of the game is a bit hazy if you haven't played the two previous installments. Some of the events and dialogue can leave you feeling questioning your self, If I were to have played the two previous games would I have a much greater understanding of what the hell these people are talking about and who they are?
PROS:
Innovative combat system that holds true to turn based combat while adding in new features to keep it as fresh as possible
Lots of character customization and combinations in terms of classes.
Despite the potential plot confusion the game's dialogue has made me chuckle, laugh or bust a gut on many occassions and was still enjoyable regardless of any confusion.

Summary: The game is an obvious throwback to the RPGs of the 16-bit era, with elements that are uniquely set to the "Penny Arcade" universe. The nostalgic appeal loses its' charm very quickly, with an intentionally incoherent storyline and script [which may appeal to fans of the series], extremely repetitive and subpar combat system, and limited exploration. However, similar to how I feel about Farcry 3: Blood Dragon, the game is very short and the main story plus bonus prelude can be completed in 6 hours without much effort. There is some replayability with the different classes available, but I personally cannot see myself replaying the main storyline since it offers little reward or enough of a altered playthrough. The game has some merit and can be a great casual play over the course of a weekend, but I would not recommend it and give it a 2/5.
Although this is the third installment in the Penny Arcade's On the Rain-Slick Precipice of Darkness, the approach is completely different in comparison to the previous games. Changing from a 3-D to sprite-based 2-D world is the most  apparent change, but there are a couple additional elements to the game. Timing attacks, button combinations, and overkills have changed in favor of classes, interrupts, and magic. Classes in the game allow for different strategies in combating the enemy and will offer the greatest amount of customization. They range from the Scholar, which utilizes various magic spells, to the Brute which favors more physical-based attacks. By the game's end you will have the ability to equip 3 classes at the same time and can various class mixtures that favor a specific play-style.  Want to build the ultimate melee hero? You can try to mash the Brute, Hobo, and Masochist classes to maximize your strength and plus up on physical attacks. Now, due to the way that MP is accrued in the game, this has some serious limitations. MP is earned throughout a battle, for each turn a character will gain one point of MP. This means that more or less 90% of your battles will follow the same pattern and will make the game extremely repetitive. For me, I had Gabe go into an attack stance, Tycho cast an Apocalypt, Jim cast a Skeleton, and Moira interrupt a monster. Could I have changed it up? Sure! But why would I purposefully choose an option that would have been less effective in those 90% of the battles I fought? I strongly believe that if the game had more of a traditional battle system, similar to the SNES Final Fantasies then it would have made the fighting system more enjoyable.
One element of the game that I thought was a positive was the use of interrupts in the game. In a sense the game is turn-based, but as you can probably see on screenshots, there is a WAIT-COMMAND-ACT phase. Once a character reaches the COMMAND point, you decide on your action and wait until the character reaches ACT for it to execute. Now some of the classes have certain abilities that will give you the ability to interrupt the enemy. For this to be effective, you have to time your character's interrupt to occur when the enemy is between the COMMAND and ACT points. If successful you can drive back the enemy's bar all the way back to the WAIT phase. This will become critical mid and late game because the more you can interrupt and slow down the enemy, the weaker the enemy will be in the long run. As the battle progresses, each turn of the enemy will yield typically a 10% increase to its' attack. This can be interpretted in two ways: either end the battle fast or prevent the enemy from acting. Certain characters, like Moira, can be class mixed to maximize her ability to interrupt the enemy and give time to the rest of the party to get a few additional actions at the beginning of the battle.
As with the previous installments, the world is rather small and the vast amount of exploration you will do in the game is limited to a a dozen dungeons. Battles are not randomnized but the types of enemy you fight will be varied and figuring out what their strengths and weaknesses can add some strategy. So the game has a set amount of battles, with pre-set monsters in each battle, and you will fight each battle at full strength [the party regenerates both items and HP after each battle]. If it isn't apparent yet, the game is linear, and each playthrough will be roughly the same as your previous playthroughs. There are only 5 playable characters in the game, of which only 4 will be useable mid to late game. As odd as it sounds, even though there are four characters, there is an extremely limited amount of character development in the game. I know of the loose associations for these characters, but there's nothing beyond that, nothing that really makes me change my opinion or gain an interest in any of the characters. Jim is a floating skull in a jar, he doesn't talk...we learn nothing new about him. Moira  was Tycho's ex-wife, we know something happened between them, but nothing is really pounded out, no flashbacks or intimate moments discussed. There may be some external source material available, but it is still the game's responsibility to draw the gamer into the world and develop a connection with the characters.
Hitting on the storyline and script, I know that there are fans out there that just love the humor and nonsensical conversations in the game, but as I played on it felt like it detracted from the game. The awkward, completely random, and  unnecessarily ornate dialogue just gave me even less to care about, the storyline is so muddled and incoherent that I found myself more confused and uncaring about the trials and tribulations of the party. I'm not asking for a 16-bit Game of Thrones, but what I would like is a storyline that makes sense...that has a purpose, an objective that is easily understood and draws me closer to the characters and plot rather than detract from it.
So in conclusion the game is mediocre at best. It has its' moments, both good and sometimes really bad, but the game has some serious flaws that limits your enjoyment. Buy it if it's very cheap, buy if you were a fan of the earlier games, but do not buy it if you're expecting to relive the glory days of the 16-bit era. The nostalgia runs out so fast, even with the Dragon Quest world and the Super Mario World-esque overworld, and when it runs out you'll realize that the game doesn't have any legitimate merits to stand on. 2/5

Note: This game was reviewed using a code sent by the developer. This is a work in progress review, I will update this review when the other episodes are released.
Lakeview Cabin 3- Review
Lakeview Cabin Collection took me by surprise once it was released. I played the original flash game and thought the idea was very interesting and had a lot of potential and then I saw that the original developer made a new game, on a bigger scale.
To begin with the game doesn't hold your hand when you start playing, you have to figure out everything by yourself otherwise you won't get anywhere.
The gameplay is simple. You take control of four campers who get attacked by serial killers and it's up to you to survive. You can set up traps or you can try and take down the killers with brute force, but it's best to take the cautious approach otherwise you won't survive.
The audio is really well done and is one of the games best features. The sound effects are awesome and sound a lot like the effects in those very cheesy slasher movies that the game is based of.
The game is overall really well made apart from a few minor bugs like characters not picking up the thing you want them to pick up.
Lakeview Cabin 3 is a really great episode and a good start to what seems to be a very promising game. I give Lakeview Cabin 3 a 8.5/10
Lakeview Cabin 4- Review
Lakeview Cabin is the second episode in the Collection.  The first episode took us to a camp site like Friday the 13th, but this time we go to a mansion and try not to get killed by a crazy cannibal family.
Lakeview Cabin 4 changes a lot of gameplay aspects from the first episode. This time you need to find 4 gas canisters to fuel up your car and escape a mansion full of crazy cannibals, but to get them you need to kill a lot of people.  Killing increases your crazy meter which makes the screen go crazy and makes more jump scares appear. Enemies are easier to kill but there's more of them and now there's stealth to avoid an even bigger threat which you can't kill so you will have to be more careful.
This episode is very interesting and it feels fresh which I like a lot. Now for the good. The audio is still really good. The gameplay is very fun and challenging which is a lot of fun. Funny like always and the graphics are awesome.
But there are a few problems. This episode was really buggy. An enemy hit me through a door which was closed, and of course the same problem where my character wouldn't pick up what I wanted to pick up. The random aspect of the episode is a great way to add replay value, but for people who have a hard time with the game might have more trouble since they can't learn from they're mistakes.
Overall it's still a very fun game and I can't wait to play Episode 3 or Lakeview Cabin 5 whatever you want to call it. It's worth the full price without a doubt. I give Lakeview Cabin 4 a 7.5/10
Lakeview Cabin 5 - Review
Taking  a detour from the previous play style of the other episodes the third episode of Lakeview Cabin takes more of a puzzle game approach. Lakeview Cabin 5 makes you play as four teenagers again in a place that is taken straight out of Halloween the movie.
The goal in this episode is quite different. You can't die this time, but you have one goal to figure out how to kill a murderer who is immortal.
As stated before this takes a more slow paced approach than the other two episodes. This time it's more about puzzle solving than anything. I liked the puzzle solving in this episode and some of the puzzles are incredibly crazy not to mention some of the solutions are absurd, but it's incredibly fun non the less.
When I began this episode, I loved the retro feel. It felt like Halloween the movie with Nightmare on Elm Street characters. This for me the best looking Lakeview Cabin Episode by far.
Now for the bad and there is a lot this time. The episode is the buggiest episode by far. I had to relaunch the episode several times after finishing one of the puzzles due to the audio cutting out after I finish it. Not to mention the very weird movement of the killer. Sometimes he doesn't attack you at all and just jitters and place.
In the end I loved Lakeview Cabin Episode 3, because of the puzzle solving aspect. In the end if the bugs weren't there I would say it's the best episode right now.
If you don't own Lakeview Cabin Collection right now, you just simply need to get it. It's one of the most fun you can have with a horror title.
Lakeview Cabin 5 gets a 8/10

As an Educational game, the main goal is to teach players about the Pleistocene (aka Ice Age), as mentioned on the description. We are guided by the history, which are established as dialogues on the foreground and background. A lot of the information are interesting facts. A lot of them couldn’t be derived from common knowledge, least without some research. Some facts include:

The game also includes a few mini-games: they range from a mix-and-match, to connect the pieces together concept, and aren’t at all challenging to play.
I like the art style of the game. The fuzzy, paint-like textures gave a nice warm feeling to the game, and is almost designed to have an outlook as that of a child’s book. The text shown in the game are also soft, with a format similar to Comic-Sans. The effects however, were kept to a minimum so there wasn’t too much happening on the screen. In the forest, we see some falling leaves, birds and moving clouds in the background. When we reach the water, we see some fish moving to and fro.
The music is also relaxing, and goes in sync with the nature of the game.
Now, I’m not sure if this game fits the category of being tagged as an Adventure game. To reach the end point of the goal will take no more than 10 seconds when you just hold the “D” key. We are also in a fairly small map, where we explore two terrains: One is forest, the other is the ocean. That is all. If there is one reason for the down votes, it would be this, and how short the entire game play is. It is not exactly one to recommend for players who enjoy the thrill of action.
I admired the art and overall concept of the game though, and give The Deer a thumbs-up. I’d suggest this game to anyone who likes playing in a short and educational, interactive game.

Легенда в своё время тоже была обновлением серии, но если бы сейчас сделали её ремастеринг, то она затмила бы недавний "перезапуск".
Что мне нравится в этой игре больше всего, так это калейдоскопическая смена декораций. Думаю пальцев на обеих руках не хватит чтобы перечислить все уголки света, в которых доведётся побывать Ларе (и вам :) На вскидку: Англия, Боливия, Япония, Непал, Казахстан, пещеры, небоскребы, гонки на мотоциклах и т. д.
Другая особенность Легенды, которая радует меня не меньше первой, - это гардеробчик Лары. Шкаф буквально ломится от обилия цветов и фасонов: около десятка базовых моделей, плюс две-три расцветки на каждую. И за всё это разнообразие не надо платить жадным издателям, вы просто получаете эти шкурки в награду за прохождение игры и выполненение заданий. Кроме того, игра не ограничивает нас рамками якобы "реализма" при повторном прохождении, и позволяет отправиться в заснеженный Непал в платьице или же в знойное Перу в полушубке.
Устаревшая графика нисколько не омрачает картину, она наоборот выталкивает геймлей на поверхность. Согласитесь, большинство современных игр маскируют унылость игрового процесса под красотами картинки.
Из всех сыгранных мною игр (АОД, Анни, Андер) эта наиболее разноплановая и содержательная.

I heard so much good about this game... But I was so disappointed by what I got.
I had high expectations for this game. It was made to sound like the best Tomb Raider game. If this really is the best, I'm never revisiting any of the games any more. There were two problems that kept me from really enjoying it:
1. Third person perspective. The camera angles at times made the game difficult to play as you can't really see very well, as Lara Croft is in the way. Third person was never my thing, but this game is worse about it than most third person titles I've played. Sometimes I need to turn the camera around, and what I end up seeing is a weird blotted screen where Croft's skin sticks out in little polygon shapes. Like how am I supposed to see with this? I can't see a thing because it keeps getting STUCK!
2. SO MANY BUGS! In fact, there's a bug that won't even let me beat the second level. It's literally not even possible. I have consulted walkthrough after walkthrough thinking maybe I did it wrong. Nope. I didn't. I can hook the  column with the ball on top of it day long and pull all the way out. It won't even budge. Also, Stretchy hair (I had this over half of the time, and it added to the aforementioned problems with the games perspective). Even Bugthesda can't rival the bugs here. Crystal Dynamics apparently can't debug a game. Sure this only had two really bad bugs, but when one of them prevents you from actually beating the game, it is beyond miserable. They were also both LESS THAN AN HOUR APART!
Honestly, this game wasn't even good to start with. The plotline is hard to follow and poorly explained. Sure I'm at the beginning, but not even being able to comprehend the plotline is inexcusable. Also, the graphics were pretty bad even for the time. MGS2 had better graphics than this. It was released 5 years earlier. Not good. What about the character lineup? Not much to say here, as the characters in general are pretty poorly developed, even for 2 hours in. I would rant, but it would have loads of spoilers. The game's puzzles were debateably too easy, and the shooting sections felt really awkward and misdone, and that didn’t help at all.
I'm not writing this to trash the game. I enjoyed the parts I could, but the bugs and the camera angles always got in the way. I can't believe this released for blockbuster prices 10 years ago, because I only payed $1.74 to play it, and I have to say it wasn't worth it. I only got a buggy game that could be played up to what's supposedly the easiest puzzle in the game . I can't believe that so many led me to waste my time. Not Bubsy bad, but still miserable.

This is very complex game, there is a lot to learn.
Oddly though, there is still no instructions or manual in game.
CRS recently made a tutorial for new Steam users - but it's useless - a clunky time-waster that teaches common basics like how to move, and how to fire.
Nothing about how to drive a truck, spawn into battle, or use an AT gun; how and why to capture a spawnable CP, the importance of an MS tick for an attack, the tactics in taking a town etc. etc.
New users must either spend time outside the game reading the wiki, forums, guides and you-tube videos - or try to learn by trial and error.
Which means many trials and many errors - most new players experience the frustration of spawning in and running towards battle, only to find it is miles away and takes literally hours to get there. A few experiences like that will send them away.
Or driving miles to a town which cannot be captured as it has no AO - but no explanations of AOs and DOs are given.
The chat channels are critical in this game, but this is not made clear. Recruits are not automatically tuned into the vital Side chat channel and are not instructed to do so - missing much comms without realising it.
Meanwhile vets get frustrated at recruits who don't know what to do, and openly abuse them for it (including in Side chat which they cannot even hear.) There is view in the CRS forums e.g. that Steam recruits are not smart enough for this game, and that the game's problems are caused by players who don't know how to play the game properly.
Over the years, CRS has suffered much criticism (some deserved, some not) and this has lead CRS into a 'bunker mentality' - they are extremely defensive about criticism. New leader Xoom is trying to do a good job, but some in his team are blind - like one who denies every single criticism of the rats or the game, every time - such as denying any problem with any weapon even while CRS is doing an audit to fix various weapon problems.
Currently, there is a problem with FMS camping which is seriously spoiling game play. The view of many vets and rats on the forum is that this is simply because new recruits are too stupid to know how to handle it. There is far more abuse and criticism than communication and co-operation. Every problem is apparently the fault of stupid players. Reports about cheaters are ignored/rejected.
There is much to like about this complicated and challenging game - but not if you simply want to jump in and have some quick & easy friendly fun.

This game is by far one of the most fantastically crafted and detailed horror games I have ever played. The fact that this game was created by a single person shocks me, for it is so detailed and so perfectly displays all of the horror movie tropes we have come to know and love through the years. To thoroughly enjoy this game you must have an imagination to craft a story for these characters, who are basically blank canvases meant to have a personality crafted for them by the player. There also is a briliantly crafted yet oddloy convoluted story that at this point has not been fully revealed due to the fact that only two episodes have been released thus far, yet if you are a person who is fit and able to search out a hidden backstory within a game will be pleasantly suprised. The gameplay is simple due to the fact that it completely revolves around a pick up and throw mechanic I have not seen in any other two dimensional pixelated indie games, yet it feels like this mechanic should have been used from the start in the horror game genre. The second episode feels like an entirely different game, due to the fact that the creator chose to go with a Texas Chainsaw Massacre approach instead of his usual Friday The 13th feel, but still proves to be as incredibly, if not even more, replayable. What the creator has accomplished thus far is incredible, being that he is a single developer who is somehow able to create a game that I, and many others would consider better than most triple a titles released this year. Few other games had me constantly checking the developers twitter for updates on the games progress, and I dont even have an account on that site. This game is so criminaly underplayed that it makes me sick. If you are a fan of anything horror related, it is a neccesity that you buy this game, and if the creator of this game sees this post, please make me a tester, for never before have I wanted to be involved in a games developement more than I would to have the privalige to help you develope this amazing game.

I love Penny Arcade and immensly enjoyed the earlier iterations of PA: OtRSPoD, but this one fell short. I like Zeboyd's idea of adding new features to the retro RPG model to make it interesting, but no ammount of innovation can possibly remove the mind-numbing tedium of those old games, and no ammount of nostalgia can make them fun. The game took me about ten hours, and that is more than double the ammount of time I'm willing to spend on such a repetitive combat system. Further, while the earlier games were funny throughout, and had amusing plot points revealed about the world of new Arcadia, this one  was only good for the occasional chuckle, and none of the plot was more interesting than stringing your characters along a series of drawn-out dungeons. Seriously, what has happened to Penny Arcade?

This game has, far and away, one of my favorite combat systems of all time. It's turn-based enough to satisfy one's desire to go at the pace you want, but dynamic enough that Speed is a relevent stat. Even if you think Penny Arcade is dumb, or if you think the name is stupid, you should play this game. If there's ever an rpg you liked even a little bit, you should play this game. If you like humor in any way, you should play this game. If you hate puns, you should probably avoid this game.

To compare this game to the original 6 Tomb Raider games would be quite unfair. They were puzzle games first, adventure games second, this one is an adventure game first and barely a puzzle game at all. That's not to say it's not as good as the first ones. Just different. And to be honest, I think we all needed a bit of change after the absolute disaster that was The Angel Of Darkness.
A bit about difficulty in this one, I don't recommend you go for the hardest difficulty because it's not balanced very well. I generally go for the hardest difficulty when I play games because I always think "The bigger the challenge, the more fun I'll have!". That's not really the case here because there was a motorcycle sequence in the Kazakhstan chapter that was absolutely impossible to get past on the hardest difficulty. I think you need to upgrade your pistols all the way in order to progress past that section by collecting enough collectibles and I just didn't want to do that. So I actually ended up restarting the game from the beginning. I managed to blow through it on the easiest difficulty back to where I was in about an hour and a half, so it wasn't the biggest deal in the world. Still, I shouldn't have to do things like that.
Also, the game is very glitchy. I made sure to not enable next generation content because I heard that causes problems but even with it off I got stuck on objects more times than I'd care to mention, fell out of the game world and into the void once, enemies would get stuck and not move, including a boss and if you're not facing the ladder directly you run the risk of climbing at the wrong angle, causing problems when you want to jump off. Not to mention that the boss dialogue had no  chill. Every boss has like 3 or 4 lines recorded that they'll say every now and then in a boss fight but something happened that caused them to just say the lines over and over and over again with no pause. The game was surprisingly buggy.
When I fired up the first Tomb Raider game I was expecting an action adventure game in the same vein as the Uncharted series and what I got was a full fledged puzzle game with a tiny bit of adventure sprinkled in. I used to resent it for that but as I went through the original 6 games I began to love it. Some times it made me feel outright stupid but I think we can all benefit from feeling stupid while playing video games every now and then.
Now with Tomb Raider: Legend I got what I originally thought I was going to get back then. I was disappointed in the original for its lack of adventure but loved it for its challenging puzzles, I was disappointed in this one for its lack of challenging puzzles but loved it for its adventure. Maybe some day we will have the best of both worlds... But it is not this day!

Remember awful controls, and horrible gameplay?  Remember how Tomb Raider was all about breasts and butts, and had little substance?  The awful jumping puzzles and all?
I started the game with all that in my head, and I was like "ok I'll give this a couple hours" About 7 hours later, I put down my controller and was pleasantly surprised.
Ok that's not entirely true either.  I had a major problem and almost gave up on this game as "unplayable" because the "next gen features" whatever they are, create a crash during a level.  I stopped playing without an intention of returning, but then I found out that turning off next gen features will allow you to skip that crash.
However outside of that crash I did have trouble putting the game down.  I had a really good time with the game.  It's not a near perfect tour de force as the "Tomb Raider" reboot was, but it isn't as big a train wreck as I remembered the series being.  I honestly think people played the original set of tomb raiders, and rarely tried the rest of the series, because up until Tomb Raider, I really don't remember many people saying positive things about this series.
Now while this is a very good (even great) game, there's one thing that should be mentioned.  There are a few driving sections that are... to put it bluntly, awful.  Everything about these sections feel off.  The controls are straight out of 2000 or earlier  (Press up to go forward on a motorcycle).  The enemies, and collisions hurt too much, the shooting is weak, one of them is heavily timed, the other doesn't appear to be (or at least isn't as strict).  The challenge is high for all the wrong reasons, and overall they are one of the only areas I can say I hated.   The only good news about them is there's two or three of them and that's it.
Besides those driving sections, the game is an incredible exploration game.  What is especially great in my mind is there were a few puzzles I felt stumped at, where I literally didn't have a clue how to progress at first, and I had to use trial and error.   It's rare for a game to really stump me and this game had a perfect blend, where I felt stumped, but I was able to puzzle it out.  I often felt I knew what was and wasn't possible, and had a clue how to solve the puzzle, but at the same time the solution wasn't laid out for me, and that was refreshing.
The story of the game is that Lara is chasing after a specific artifact, it's an artifact that has a link to her past, and the disappearance of her mother, I don't want to give away what it is or the story, but it's a solid tale that kept my attention, even as it went a little too heavily into the mysticism.   There's a few people who assist Lara, who don't get a ton of development (apparently their back story is in the prequel, Tomb Raider Anniversary) but are always there to drop a hint or a timely quip over the coms, as this is a solo affair.
If you can get over the 2006 graphics (which has aged, but still feels acceptable), the awful bike levels (few, but noticibly bad) and don't mind a little cheesiness in the dialog, this is an easy recommendation.  It's a 7 dollar game, that's easily worth that price, or more.  It has a memorable story, and fantastic level design.   It also contains great locations, and gameplay.   Overall I think Tomb Raider: Legends should have got the same level of attention that the newest Tomb Raider has.  The newer game is definitely better, delivering a more fleshed out character and story, and a better game, but at the same time, you can still go back and play Legend before or after it and enjoy it, for the excellent adventure it offers.

Xenonauts is in essence an X-COM game after the spirit of the orignal title. I enjoyed the recent Firaxsis XCOMs and, obviously, they are graphically superior to Xenonauts, however Xenonauts has a greater depth of strategic play. Like in the original X-COM, Time Units allow your soldiers to perform complex tasks on the battlefield and this puts paid to my biggest beef with the Firaxsis games. Just like in olden times Soldiers can now shoot then move then crouch and turn, open doors and reload and these actions can be performed in any order as long as there are sufficient time units available to them. No longer will a reload always end my turn and no longer do I need a soldier with a special skill to be able to shoot then move! This alone makes Xenonauts eminently playable for anyone interested in the genre and is one of many areas that the game gets right.

To compare Xenonauts to XCom series would be the easiest, but also unfair way to deal with this enormous strategy. Quite certainly and without any shame, Xenonauts developers Goldhawk Interactive are speaking out the truth about their inspiration - Xenonauts is spiritual successor of acclaimed strategic game XCom: UFO Defense.
Gameplay resolves in circles which comprises of three main elements: management of your bases and strategic command centers via Geoscape, your game screen; real-time air combat and final stage - turn based ground combat.
Although we live in cruel time when hand drawn graphics are unfairly judged as unworthy by most of the (childish) players, get over retro, but charming hand-drawn sprites and you'll enter the world of comprehensive, multilayered strategy where you can manipulate every single aspect of your gaming experience. Numerous classes, weapons, tactics, strategies, upgrades and ideas have been brought upon the table and shrouded in mystery and atmosphere which perfectly collides panic of alien invasion and Cold war isolation.
There are numerous selling points to Xenonauts, but one of the most important IS and SHOULD BE that it's an honorable, greatly improved over original and richer hommage to XCom which delivers in every single aspect. It's unbeliveable that an indie team can deliver a game that even surpasses the original on so many fields.
If you're into aliens and hungry for some long-lasting strategic battles that will test your nerves, luck and decisions, go for it.

Usually, when you hear the phrase Horror Comedy, what is being described is a comedy with the dressings of horror.  Movies like Tucker and Dale vs Evil or Shaun of the Dead aren't so much scary as they are kind of gross or gory sometimes, but the comedy is solid and the movies themselves are excellent.
Lakeview Cabin is a unique example of the genre.  When someone says Lakeview Cabin is Horror Comedy, what they mean is that it epitomizes both separate genres equally.  Lakeview Cabin is tense and freaky and, in general, simply excellent at that Horror trick of making you do something while every part of your body tells you not to, especially considering its crude, pixelly style (or, perhaps, partially because of it).  Your heart will race as you try to execute that last, desperate plan to save your own skin as an immortal serial murderer bares down on you in the dark.  At the same time, the freedom it allows the player in its little sandbox levels, combined with the game's swift, incredibly violent consequences of poor decision making, almost immediately opens up a world of hugely bloody, absurd comedy.  In few other games can you run to pick up a shotgun and blast a monster in the face only to discover it is empty, and the only other nearby object is a small pug which has been wandering the island carefree for days now, and in no other games can you desperately pick up that pug and try to hurl it at your killer's face, only for it to soar into a nearby running woodchipper instead, spraying blood and bits of bone at a hapless friend standing nearby.
The game has a sick and hilarious sense of humor, and, at the same time, is thrilling, tense, and off-puttingly weird.  Is that pregnant redneck trapped in the attic the source of all these slimy, bloodthirsty creatures slithering and snuffling through the walls?  Is that a man-sized, deformed infant careening around the island with a knife?  What are they doing with all these chickens?  What is that thing in the lake, and what did it do to our dog?  What are those two naked twins doing in the bathroom with that dessicated corpse?  These are but a tiny fraction of the worrying questions you'll pose to yourself while playing Lakeview Cabin Collection.
If you're at all a fan of weird sandbox titles, 70s grindhouse horror flicks, horror in general, comedy, combinations of the two, solving puzzles, playing games, or being a cool person, you should strongly consider giving this a shot.

Serious Sam can be considered the epitome of old-school FPS games: 100% pure action, non-linear levels filled with secrets, and hundreds upon hundreds of monsters to kill with a vast arsenal. Mindless first-person combat has rarely been this fun.
When CroTeam, this small Croatian studio released Serious Sam: The First Encounter in 2001, probably even they didn’t think that their game will grow into one of the most successful indie FPS franchises. After all, on the surface, it looks like any other shooter from around 2000: half-linear levels where it is impossible to get lost yet have enough room to hide many secrets, all full of pickups to supply the player with health and ammo for the sizeable arsenal.
The trick is that this simplicity hides excellent game mechanics. The action rarely stops, but it doesn’t try to tire out the player by not giving enough breathing room. The difficulty levels offer a balanced challenge to FPS newbies and grizzled veterans alike. (Just to illustrate: on ‘Serious’ difficulty, you meet over six thousand enemies during the course of the game.)
The range of difficulties is only overshadowed by the available option in the engine itself. The Serious Engines were always famous of letting the player take control, but the first one really takes the top. Thanks to this awesome flexibility, the game ran on anything back then and looks surprisingly good even today, despite its old age.
I’d lie if I said CroTeam put too much effort in the story: you play as Sam Stone, who was sent back to the source of all evil, ancient Egypt, to stop an alien warlord from eradicating humanity in the far future. Still, the writing is quite memorable, thanks to the corny one-liners and the overall nonsensical nature of some of the encounters that help to alleviate the stress after some especially adrenaline-pumping scenario. So, in a sense, the “story” does its job, like the rest of the game.
