Xenonauts is a wonderful clone of the original XCOM - UFO DEFENSE and is in many ways a better experience. Xenonauts is more intuitive and pretty than its predecesor as well as creating the same feeling that you are juggling 9001 balls at once, and are constantly a few poor choices away from total collapse. All in all, the game is a great experience.
Although I have not completed the game, just scratched the surface really (I've played three months in-game), I can say for certain that all of the difficulty of the original game is present. Every desicion is vital and it is imperative to really consider the best course of action at all times. If you don't, well, let's say there have been more than a few missions which resulted in complete annihilation of my squad, a terrible loss.
The game is also much more faithful to the original than XCOM - ENEMY UNKNOWN, bringing back TU's, much larger squads, and a more complicated geoscape portion of the game. In many respects, though, it improves on the original. The OP Blaster bomb has been removed, the graphics look polished and attractive, and useful/relevant data is more easily accessed.
However, I do not mean to say that the game is without faults. For new players to the series, there is hardly and tutorial to introduce them to the many facets of being an international super-secret alien defense force commander. This means the learning curve can be quite steep. Furthermore, the game has some frustrating line of sight issues. Sometimes, I will attempt to move my soldier to firing position, only to discover that the bush I was trying to shoot through might as well be a solid wall. Although over time I have been able to more successfully ascertain what I can and can't do, it has provided a great deal of frustration.
All in all, the game is excellent, and in my oppinion more pleasurable to play than the original. (Although the punishing nature of the original adds a bit to the feel. Ironically by making it better it's worse?) Anyway, if you are a fan of strategy games or the original series then I would highly recommend you purchase this game immediately and begin fighting off the extraterrestrial invasion!

Had this on PS3 and after playing Tales from the Borderlands... I had to play this again,

Pros

Cons

That said, my biggest peeve with this game; Balance. I believe its the hunters pack 2, but one of the Xpacs/expansions "scales" enemies to your level. I was able to clear the TVHM campaign with a bit of issue toward the end, but then decided to try and tackle Tinas campaign (the only one I didn't finish in normal).... and all hell broke loose. Enemies drastically outpowered me (I had all purples at level 50 from the key chest, but still got destroyed). Some areas I would die 10+ times attempting to clear just a few trash mobs... it was horrible. Looking up online, I'm not the only one who had issues; essentially unless you were willing to go "diablo mode" and go grind out specific enemies for hours to try for certain drops, your screwed. I wouldn't mind this if I were able to scale back to normal and clear Tinas.... but there was no benefit to that other than achievements. The games "balance" is just attrocious; I got to the point I actually stopped at the end of Tinas, there was some level 55 Orc dude that kept following me around everywhere one shotting me. Oh, and if you scale back, you have to reaccomplish things; sadly, unlike D3, your story progress is separate between the difficulty levels.
Yes, I would recommend this game. I loved it on PS3, and love it now. But whatever tweeks they did to the balance through the Xpacks and other things screwed the pooch IMO; I have never given up on a game for being too hard. But BL2 takes "too hard" and makes it unfair to the point you cannot progress; when your struggling with the second best tier of items in areas you are the same level as, what the hell?

I don't normally write reviews for games, but frankly ASTRONEER caught me off guard in a way i wasn't expecting.
I've played survival games up the♥♥♥♥♥♥ and some i've stuck with, some i've refunded, some i played for a bit and then never touched again, but with ASTRONEER i was instantly in love with the way it presented itself, bugs and all.
Sure, the game is nowhere near complete - once you've researched every blueprint and built everything there isn't anything to do, but this is obviously still to come, and i get the feeling that the future of this game is going to be especially bright.
I've poured hours into straight sessions just listening to the bubbling of materials into my  backpack and the lovely bloopy soundtrack that really does add a level of polish to the game.
The visuals are wonderful too, with a polygonal/minimalist design that works superbly. You have your more graphically intensive examples of games like this, but frankly it doesn't need it and delivers itself brilliantly.
The game does have its bugs like dropping items through floors, some of which i know were addressed in a recent patch, as well as some of the vehicle bay physics being slightly off once the spaceship gets involved... but these are easy fixes that will no doubt be dealt with swiftly through the Early Access phase (hopefully!)
If you want a nice, relaxing but slightly cerebral survival game that could basically be described as "Yes Man's Sky" then this game is for you. If that description repulses you to your core, i understand - but maybe try it anyway!

This game has truly passed the test of time with shining colors. CS:GO blends a simple concept with an incredible sense of strategy and gameplay.
Pros:
-Weapons require intense practice to handle properly, with each requiring hours upon hours to master
-Movement can be improved and perfected by learning to "bunny-hop", which provides a significant advantage
-Spray patterns for most weapons are constant and controllable
-Players are forced to play strategically, and mistakes are easily punished
-Communication is vital to victory
-Grenades are constant and effective when used properly and are an essential part of any push or hold
-Teamwork is a must and can change the tide of almost any scenario
-Dropped weapons can benefit the opposing team, making players choose weapons wisely
-Great reliance on map knowledge
-Great reliance on game sense
-Fast reaction times are rewarded
-Proper aim can be mastered and perfected
-Positioning is key to victory
-Wide variety of weapons requires players to be effective with all weapons in all scenarios
Cons:
-Competitive ranks seem unrewarding and sometimes incorrect
-Weapon skins
-Community includes all types of people (Good and Bad) [unavoidable in any online game]
-Spray patterns when jumping/running/climbing are unpredictable and seem unfair to die from
-Playing on anything other than an exclusively Prime match will most likely result in a cheater of some sorts
-Some weapons seem out of place (Negev/M249 have almost no place in a strategic playstyle & the Sawed Off shotgun does not have a place other than extremely close range, in which Counter-Terrorists should not engage in)
Take my opinion with a grain of salt if you disagree, but I would most definitely recommend this game to anyone.

When you're playing WWII Online, just remember that it's not like other games. If you were even the slightest curious about Crystal Dynamics first take on Lara and the Tomb Raider series, you should definitely give this a go.  Released during the Playstation 2 and Xbox era, Crystal Dynamics provided a fresh, modern, and polished take on a series that had almost been long forgotten.
It is in many ways a precursor to the Playstation's Nathan Drake series and even the recently rebooted Tomb Raider series.  Where 2013's Tomb Raider is gritty, grounded in some realism - Tomb Raider: Legend features a tone similar to that of the original series developed by Core Design.  The aesthetic is more comic than it is realistic and Lara is not without her great one-liners.
The adventure is over quickly, but you will still have Anniversary and Underworld to play through - which continue the storyline that begins here.

Superb climbing/jumping mechanics and level design. Combat is kinda weird at first but once you understand it it's pretty fun. Also Lara is a badass. The cartoonish characterizations work in favor of the modern fantasy universe they went for.

Well, after completing the game because my nostalgia got the better of me, I must say that it isn't entierly what I was expecting. Hear me out, I remembered the game being a lot longer and a lot more difficult when I was younger. Ok, so maybe that's because I'm not the MLG OpTic FaZe master that I am now, but still, it took a little over 10 hours to complete the whole game, from start to finish.
There are 6 characters that you can play as in the game;
-Sonic basically goes from start to finish as fast as he can, but with no time limits or anything. He is the only character with 15 stages, everyone else has 5.
-Tails wants to be faster than Sonic, so he uses flight to get in front of Sonic, and if he is too slow, too bad, the game ends and you lose a life.
-Knuckles takes hardly any time at all, because the levels are small, and he only wants to find 3 peices of a master emerald that are poorly hidden. It is hardest to find them when they are inside an enemy, because you don't generally care to kill them after your second or third campaign.
-Amy runs from her babysitter. A lot.
-Big is the shortest campaign by far, because he needs to catch his frog, who can LITERALLY BE FOUND AT THE BEGINNING OF EVERY LEVEL. Still, it will take at least 10 minutes on the first stage for you to figure out that you need to mash random buttons in order to reel in 'froggy.' However, he would be a True Pacifist if he played Undertale, because he literally needs to kill nobody. Even the final boss. Really.
-E-102 is your average aimbot hacker who uses a laser to mark targets and increase the countdown timer he has to deal with for some reason. He's actually pretty fun to play, but he is also extremely easy to play. Go into a room with a bunch of enemies, spin around a few times, and everybody is dead. To be honest, his campaign is actually pretty good, and hollywood could make a movie out of his story.
Ok, so the nostalgia doesn't quite live up to my expectations. So what? It's f*#7ing Sonic Adventure, a game many of us grew up with, and I think it's OK. Rather short, but OK. On this runthrough, I didn't bother with the Chao that many of us know and love, mainly because none of the eggs that I was told would hatch actually did so. So if you're looking to ONLY do the campaign, you have about 10 hours of gameplay that you will only die in because of either the game's fault, you are too young to be good, or you are new to gaming. No matter what, you will probably be laughing at how bad some of the cutscenes are and some of the faces the characters make.
So, yeah. Buy it if it's on sale in that Sonic games collection thingy. You won't be dissapointed.*
*'Dissapointed' refers to it's literal meaning, not it's figurative meaning. If you ARE Dis-a-point-ed, please see a doctor immediately.

It's an interactive picture book for small children. Something where you take your three-year-old onto your lap, and go, "Oh, look, a deer!" and let the kid pick out  more things and naming them, as well as you reading the text to them.
Think the short books with thick cardboard pages you may have at home or find in the doctor's waiting room. As that, it does the job nicely.
Unlike with a cardboard book, here your child can move the deer back and forth, and play a few simple minigames; memory, a type of jigsaw, and pick the right objects from an image. (If you set a key for vertical movement, you can even make the deer vanish.)
And that's it. I can imagine plenty of entertainment value for a small child (I met a few in my life), at the age where they like to go through always the same picture book, and get a giggle out of (wrongly) suggesting to feed the deer chips and chocolate.
For what it is, I recommend it. Others just need to consider whether they'd pick up a cardboard book of the same price for a child at the right age.

Tomb Raider Legend has an interesting storyline (although I don't really think it matters any more since the series has been rebooted again). The game offers a wide range of environments to explore, with each level taking place at a different country, and the game-play seems to vary depending on the level, as some level focus more on attacking enemies, while other level focus on traditional tomb raiding and action adventure. Since this entry was supposed to be the reboot of the Tomb Raider franchise, a lot of changes were made. Some are good and some are not very good. Legend is just very different from Core Design's classic Tomb Raider games overall.
However, I have to warn you that this game is very, very SHORT. [Light Spoiler] It contains only 7 major levels and the Croft Manor. In fact,  I think it is the same length as Tomb Raider Chronicles or maybe even shorter. Furthermore, TR Legend only presents the first halves of the Tomb Raider Trilogy story as the second halves of the story is told in Underworld.  To make up for this, this game does contain a lot of bonus contents and secrets.
My advice is that if you are new to the series because of Tomb Raider (2013), and you are interested in a game with interesting story , you should play it. If not, you should probably wait for it to be on sale again.

Key Features:
All-New Characters and All-New Classes: Four all new playable classes including the Siren, the Commando, the Gunzerker and the Assassin. Step into the role of the Gunzerker, whose highly deadly skills allow him to dual-wield any two weapons found in the game. Not only that, you will build on that skill to do more things with two guns than you ever imagined possible. Dual machine guns? Cool. Dual rocket launchers? Of course! Dual Sniper Rifles? Dynamic Co-op online, and LAN: Share your adventures with friends both online and via LAN. Borderlands 2 features a seamless system enabling you to drop in and drop out of a campaign without ever having to restart the game. On top of that you can even take your new gear from any game to any other!
World Connected Story: Find yourself left for dead in the frozen tundra of Pandora as you begin your quest of revenge and redemption. Expose the evil surrounding the Hyperion Corporation and take on the perpetrator of a universe-wide grand deception -- the nefarious Hyperion CEO, Handsome Jack. 87 Bazillion...Everything: In addition to the new gun system, you will lust after procedurally generated shields, grenades, Relics, class mods and much, much more. And you thought the original Borderlands had a ton of loot!
Brand new environments on Pandora: Hunt through entirely brand new areas of Pandora that are more alive than ever! From the arctic tundra, through the dangerous grasslands, past the mysterious corrosive caverns to beyond, you’ll be surprised by the unpredictable world of Pandora at every turn!
Brand new enemies: A whole slew of new enemies are out there to kill you in Borderlands 2. Hulking, gorilla-like Bullymongs, vicious predatory Stalkers and the Hyperion mechanical army, run by Handsome Jack, are just some of the new enemies in Borderlands 2.

the game difficulty curve never changes, and there is nothing you can do get ahead of it. Your troops never even get as good as the aliens troops, they are ALWAYS better, faster, more accurate.
The aliens are ALL snipers (even the blind ones). They can shoot through glass, over obstacles and kill your troops in one hit easily on normal. Additionally, shots are % based on your total time units, so your troops NEVER get to fire more shots per round, just move further.
The reaction fire system makes it almost impossible to kill any aliens without getting shot yourself by the alien who's turn it ISN'T, because all the aliens seem to have AMAZING reaction times.
2 Months into the game you need 4 bases and 20 fighter craft to deal with the entire worlds ufo problems and you will only have money 1\5 of that. Ufo invasions come in literal swarms so your ships sit and wait or are outnumbered 3 to 1.
Scientists and engineers can NOT be moved from base to base, they must be fired and re-hired.

After the grand disapointment that Firaxis delivered in the form of X-com: Enemy Unknown and the slightly better game that came afterwards. I was looking for a game that had more focus on the strategy, the base building, on the various aspects of running a company that is the sole defence against aliens.
Xenonauts delivers, and though it was rather buggy in various of the alpha stages, the game has matured and become an all round great game to play.
You've got base management to focus on, every structure you build having a goal and purpose.
There's research and development going on, getting your troops better armor and weapons, or upgrading the weapons on your aircraft, researching and manufacturing newer ships to fight the aliens with.
Every soldier has a large variety of stats that upgrade and increase the more missions you play with the, and that progression really makes a difference, making every soldier a more and more valuable asset, making losing them that much more bitter when it does happen.
But that's fun, because unlike Firaxis's itterations of the game, where you were always pushed into certain behaviors to be the most efficient. Xenonauts offers you a lot more flexibility right from the start.
You have the whole world to defend, you can start wherever you want with your base and develop your team towards your ideal. Various types of grenades and a whole list of weapon types give you complete control over the battlefield, over what you want your soldiers to do and how you want them to evolve.
The game isn't easy though, because like the older generation it's based on, things can simply go wrong, an alien enemy with poor eye sight might still one of your own men by chance, and the results could be deadly! Good tactics help you out though, good preparation and positioning allowing you to jump enemies before they can possibly respond to your actions.
This is a fantastic game, especially if you loved the older games. The strategy, the management, the ufopedia, it's all very well put together, giving you a great time all around.

Eversion is a platformer in the vein of Super Mario Bros. (to the point that the game files call the enemies "goombas", and an achievement makes reference to the first SMB). On the subject of Achievements, those, leaderboards for a "time attack" mode, and graphical improvements are what you're actually paying for in this Steam release; the developer, Zaratustra Productions, also has a freeware version available at their site,
.
According to the manual (available from the game's Steam Store page), you are Zee Tee, a brave -a-s-t-e-r-i-s-k- warrior, out to save the Flower Kingdom's Princess -N-e-h-e-m-a-, -k-i-d-n-a-p-p-e-d- by the Ghuliba forces of the north. Aside from that, there's not much explicit story to be had. However, as per the game's title, there are many layers to this quaint little story, just as there are layers to the world itself. Along with the jumping around, jumping on enemies, jumping to headbutt blocks established with SMB and its kin, the eversion mechanic allows you to evert at certain places on the stages, changing how the stage behaves. The physics will always stay the same, but stage elements and enemies will shift with the peeling layers of reality.
And you'll need to evert, too, to get everything there is. There are 240 gems to collect, and nabbing all these buggers will push your reflexes and understanding of the game's mechanics to get yourself to where they are. There tend to be at least a couple ways to accomplish these feats, though, which opens it up a bit for experimentation.
I definitely like the graphics boost this version has over the freeware. The added detail really brings out what you're seeing, and keeps it from becoming "just a bunch of sprite tiles". The only sacrifice is one if you prefer simplicity, especially during the endings (oh, yes, there's more than one ending to find), but I don't think the little flourishes diminish the effect the game gives. The music helps with the effect, though it may get on your nerves if you end up in a stage too long. However, until that point, they're pretty catchy, with a technical level that matches the retro aesthetic the game's made with. And both will help you find the eversion points, as these nexuses will blend the sounds and colors of the layers they lead to.
As for the challenge, I think you'd have to know if you're compatible with platformers to play this one. If you're cool with the run-&-jump, you should be able to get through to an ending with enough effort, though to truly delve into everything, you may end up offput, but not enough to drive you away from the game permanently. The levels, aside from the first, have checkpoints midway through the stage, though if you quit the stage, you'll have to begin from the top. Some stages require precise jumping (with one calling for vertical block-scaling, jumping from one block to one directly above it) or races against time, and compiled with the other stage dangers, you can end up falling to your quick death many times (each time resetting the music, to boot). The game's not too terribly long, though, at less than ten stages (with a couple as part of the Time Attack mode), so if you're especially good at platformers, you may end up breezing through. And for any skill level, have some solace that your gems (and hidden 'items'; one per stage) are saved as soon as you grab them, so if you die, you don't lose your loot.
Despite how much time you get out of it, at five dollars, it's not a bank-buster, and I like what the game does to recommend it to anyone willing, whether they go with the freeware or Steam release (though if you're letting a friend play on your account, you may want to move your .sav file somewhere else and let them have a fresh start). It won't warp your brain, but it can make you uncomfortable/insecure in the game's world, and for whatever frustrations it gives, I did have a smile on when calling out on the game's ridiculous "bullcrap" moments.
Just, just keep in mind: this is "not suitable for children or those of a nervous disposition." *wink*
NOTE: My Steam profile reads me as having 11 hours on this game, but some amount of that time was just goofing around or showing it to my folks (because, really, it's that neat).

I have owned this game for awhile back when it was an early access title, back before the official XCOM reboot released. At the time I recommended not purchasing the game due to its significant list of missing features, bugs, and poor gameplay. My review of course got condemed, but I'm a true believer in reviewing a game on how it is *now* and not what it *might* become in the future.
Over a year later, here we are at the official release.
Now that the game is officially finished and released I am re-doing my review to reflect on how the game is in the current state.
Xenonauts takes the conecpt and gameplay that many of us fell in love with long ago with the DOS game X-Com: UFO Defense and brings that into the modern world. It isn't a direct copy however. The aliens are different, their are different weapons, different technologies, different aircraft. It takes the best of the original game, and combines it with some of the best modifications to that game. As icing on the cake, it also incorporates some of the features the XCOM reboot by Firaxis had.
It keeps the isometric 2D view from the original game, but with more modern graphics. Large squad sizes are present (your first aircraft can have 8). Base defense is present. You are allowed, and required, to have multiple bases. Combat remains turn-based, and time units are very much present. That convers just about all of the complaints series fans had with the XCOM Enemy Unknown reboot.
New is a more indepth aircraft interception mini-game (that's optional, you can auto-resolve if you wish). Unlike most games with an auto-resolve feature, this one doesn't screw you over with excessive losses/damage if you use it.
For anyone who was a fan of the original XCOM: UFO Defense game, or new people who don't want to deal with a DOS Box game I reccomend they check out this game and give it a shot. The initial difficulty spike is quite large, but after a few games you can learn what works for you and really start to dig in.

So, as you can see, I've played a fair bit of this game. Anyone who is into simulators and trucks can see why.
I like to take games like these serious, as if I was actually behind the wheel of that beast of a truck, hauling that heavy trailer with important cargo on it that just HAS to arrive in time, while also making sure to keep to the speed limits and not hit anything or anyone!
Here are the basic rules:
Yes, yes. I know, I know. But it's a simulator, right? It's meant to simulate, as best as possible, what it's like to do this for real? Well, I like to really immerse myself in these types of games. So, of course I'm going to worry about causing an accident! I don't want to ruin people's days, or♥♥♥♥♥♥off the client. Or spend half that money I just made from this job to repair my truck because I was too careless!
Well no, not quite. It's not really too expensive. Even less so when you get more experienced, level up your skills and therefore earn more money for a job, considering you're a more valuable driver. However, the prices can get high if you're stupid enough to race at around 90 mph down the motorway, and think you can take the turn-off at around 70-80. At that point, you're likely to crash into the barriers several times, and maybe even flip your truck. Even if you're lucky enough to not flip, your engine will malfunction. You'll be cruising along, at a cosy 60 mph, all of a sudden your engine shuts down, an error message pops up on your dash and your truck basically does an emergency stop.
. So, after a crash that caused quite a bit of damage, you can choose to risk your engine constantly going off, or you can call a tow truck that will take you to the nearest town/city. Obviously that will cost you, both money and time! So do be careful when you drive  around, especially with an urgent and important delivery!
Having said all that, sometimes it's kinda fun to just mess around. Who doesn't like to find out what it's like to drive through town at 70 mph?! If you have enough cash, and are willing to waste some, go right ahead and see just how fast that new truck you just bought can really go!
Of course, you can also upgrade and customize your truck. There are Service Stations in every city (that I'm aware of). There, you can make repairs to your truck, like replacing your tires that are starting to wear out. Go to a Service Station, select "Service" and a list will come up on the right side. It will list all the parts of your truck, what their damage is, and what it costs to repair it. All of the parts are automatically selected for repair, however you can pick and choose what you want to repair. Just note, whenever something has suffered too much damage, it will cause you problems. Just like in the real world! If your tires wear out too much, it will be more difficult to control your truck, since you won't have the traction that shiny new tires do. If you don't repair your engine, it will malfunction at random times and shut down. That can be several times in 1 minute, or happen once every 10 minutes. I'm not sure what will happen with the other parts, but I can guess that it's not going to make for a very comfortable and enjoyable drive...
To upgrade and customize your truck, go to a Service Station, and select Upgrade Shop. This will bring you to another screen where you can select a new Cab, Chassis, Engine, Transmission, Left or Right Steering Wheel, Paint, Outside Accessories and Inside Accessories. When you select either of the Accessories, some gray dots will appear on certain parts of your truck. Clicking on one will display parts on the list to the left. Hovering over a part will show you what it will look like on your truck. Clicking on it will install it.
Once you're finished, confirm your order at the bottom of the list and all the changes you've made will be saved. If, however you want to remove something from your order, just click on "See Changes", and select the part/s you want to remove, or just clear your order.
Once you've confirmed your order, you can leave the menu and see that beautiful new truck you've just spent the last hour creating! Why not take a screenshot and share it?
Another thing you can do is connect your profile to World of Trucks. You will have the option to sign into your account, or make a new one in-game. Once you've done that, you can go to the World of Trucks website. There you can set up your profile, see your truck stats for both ETS2 and ATS, as long as they are both connected to your account. You will also be able to change your licence plate number, for both games. Choose which Country/State the plate is from, then enter whatever you like. If you take pictures of your truck in-game through the Picture Mode, you will be able to see them in the Picture Manager in-game. There you can select which pictures to upload to your WoT account, and which one you'd like to set as a profile picture (the picture for that game, where you will see the truck stats). Whenever you upload a picture, anyone will be able to see it. Logged in users will also be able to like, favourite and comment on your picture, so remember to keep your pants on and smile before you take a selfie!
Once you've explored the game enough, you have your company set up, several garages and people working for you, bringing in so much cash you can basically move to Hawaii and retire. Or you've just got the hang of the controls of the game, but you don't like the idea of playing this awesome game all by yourself, then you can try and find a multiplayer mod for this. Personally, I use TruckersMP. You can use it with both American Truck Simulator, and Euro Truck Simulator 2. It uses your save game, so you will have everything you do in the single player version, but in multiplayer!
Of course you can also use mods through the Steam Workshop. Personally, I use mods that remove traffic, and I also got a mod that gives me a lot of XP. That way I will have all the parts unlocked in the Upgrade Shop and spend the next 2 hours going through all the new parts and paint jobs, and then try to make a truck that I'm proud to drive around the EU.
Just note that TruckersMP has some rules around mods, so any mods that are through the Steam Workshop will be disabled when launching the game with TruckersMP!

The gameplay overall is astonishingly diverse with only 4 classes. On top of all of this, the DLC feels like 4 whole seperate games, and that is how I feel all DLC should be portrayed as. Great game, and I would rate it 10/10. Amazing job Gearbox and 2K Studios.

Borderlands 2, for those that aren't familiar with the series, is somewhat of a combination of a loot based shooter and an RPG, containing levels and skill trees, but having shooter mechanics like aiming, accuracy, bullet speed, etc. The game has 6 playable characters (2 from DLC), each with their own playstyle. Also, the game manages to have an interesting story. But don't worry, if you don't care about stories, there's plenty for you. The gameplay is action packed, and is different depending on the character you are using, and the writting is witty and the level design is interesting (with few escort missions, compared to the hundreds in the game). However, the game on it's own (without the campaign extentions and extra characters) will leave you wanting more (towards the endgame, due to lack of legendaries. So, if you are going to buy this game, BUY THE GAME OF THE YEAR EDITION. AND the community is awesome.

This is truly an amazing game, one of the best of all time in my opinion. Play however you want with the 6 different characters and 3 skill trees for each, no playthough should be the same. Play as a sniper with Zer0, Dual weild two rocket launchers with Sal or smash your enemies with chainsaws strapped with dynamite as Krieg. The landscapes are beautiful and diverse, travel around them on foot or in one of two customisable vehicles (more with DLC!). With many unique skins for each character, plenty of vault symbols to find in each map and a range of bosses to fight and extra challenges in each map, you will never be out of things to do. While I believe the loot system of Borderlands 1 was better, Borderlands 2 has so many guns with 4 different elements, plus explosive and normal weapons, almost everything you find has some use at the first few levels, and as you progress you will need to start selecting what weapons will be useful for each situation, until you understand how everything works and know what iteams to take and what to leave naturally. The DLCs are unique too, one will bring you to a dried up ocean where you work with a pirate to find a hidden treasure, the next you will work your way up the ranks and become champion of the crater of badassitude, then travel to the hunters grotto to hunt some of the rarest creatures pandora has to offer before ending off in a mystical world on the hunt for an evil sorcerer and save the Queen! Not to mention the Headhunter add-ons or Gigistruct OP levels. One of the only problems is the difficulty when you hit Ultimate Vault Hunter mode, basically enemies get x4 health and the relience on slag becomes more annoying than fun, apart from that I cant think of anything wrong with the game.
9.9/10 definitly buy this, still has people on PC playing today, at all levels!

Despite it's minimalist graphic style, Prison Architect is a deep management game, with lot of hiden contents, so each time you play you will discover new management skill. It's not just about building a prison, it's about about managing prisonners behavior, finance, security (including confidential informants), food, electricity and water, because things can goes really really bad in your prison if you don't care about it... for example :  I had a confidential informant, a night I active him to follow my security agent to the security room, then he show us a prisoner which is known in all the prison as a police confidential informant, so all prisoners wants to kill him. So I change this prisoner as a Protective Custody for a better protection.
Two days later, this prisoner was killed in the canteen, under my security camera. The killers have been put in high-security quarters.
So you got to manage prisoners who are in danger too, by building special quarters for them, to avoid contact with others prisoners, like in a canteen. You can do that by managing their time regime planning, and make special zones for them.
If you want more, you can still unlock some extra features in the options menu, like weather management (including hot water pipes and radiators), gangs and staff needs. You can put phones in tapping, you can put metal gates detectors, you can have educativ training... just maybe the construction mode is a bit short (there's not so much diversity in what you can build).
Anyway, this game worth its mini-price, if you like build and management games.

This game is amazing, I spent the best month of my gaming life on it. The first week is brutal, even after the tutorials everything is hard to wrap your head around - there are no killcams, no way to see if you've killed someone or not and no way to heal.
But that's the part I love about it, it's fantastically realistic yet still so fun. Taking part in massive
offences gives you the best feeling in the world, especially when you are charging with 10-100 other men across an open field accompanied with tanks, trucks and relentless enemy fire, believe me, that happens.
You don't get taught how to drive, my advice is to look it up instead of asking for help on how to drive in the chat, you'll learn way faster.
The player base is amazing, everyone is very helpful, cooperative and a team player, there are barely and if not no cheaters and everything's fair game.
My only gripe is the subscription based payment, it is really off-putting and once your free month is up you can only play certain types of things. I feel that paying only once to get full access will be a lot more inviting, and only premium should be subscription based. The feeling of not being able to play certain units even after leveling up so much in one month is pretty soul crushing.
Nevertheless, the game is amazing and I urge anyone looking for a unique first person shooter to play this game.
Even though I could only play for a month, it was the best month of my life and really brightened up my life as I looked forward to playing it at the end of each day.

Its dated graphics, clunky controls, and somewhat steep learning curve can lead to a rough few opening minutes in the game. Dont give up! This is not a BF1 or COD. It is a deep and thoughtful simulation. Since its original launch, it has provided me with some of my most memorable gaming memories.
I recall lying in a field clutching my rifle as two opposing armored columns converge on my position, rounds flying overhead, the din of battle drowning out all other sounds. From my position i could see the enemy infantry dismounting trucks to the rear of the enemy armor. From my exposed position, i began picking them off, secure in the knowledge that they would never look for a sniper lying in the open with only tracer fire and smoke to conceal me. I lay there, tanks dueling all around me, enemy infantry falling as I squeezed off my shots.
I dont recall how many of my targets fell. I never saw the errant tank round that ended me. I just recall the whole scenario that played out over 10 years ago.
Its that kind of memory that keeps me coming back and its one of many. From dogfighting above contested cities to taking part in an armored assault, this game is gaming memory machine.
Use the training resources in game to get your footing. Locate an active battle and spawn in. Join a squad to REALLY get solid guidance and advice. In short order you will find yourself engaged.
I cannot recommend this game enough for any simulation, history buff. I have played from its original launch day and keep coming back. I cant think of any other game that has pulled me back so many times and for so long as this.

Overall rating: 6/10 - This game can be fun to mess around in and try out the missions, but it is so poorly made.
The floors and walls barely work; a simple spindash gives enough speed to go through most walls.
-Sonic's gameplay gives you some high-speed action and some puzzle solving. 7/10 - I would rate this gameplay higher, but it is very prone to glitches. Level design is questionable at some parts.
-Tails' gameplay is quite fun. Granted that you can skip most of every level just by flying straight past everything, it has an interesting design. 7/10 - Tails' story is quite short and includes TWO near back-to-back Sky Chase levels that you have to go through. Other than that, it is quite fun.
-Knuckles' gameplay is trash. Knuckles barely functions in this game. The controls are bad, the emerald arenas are bad and the story is boring. 3/10 - Knuckles has quite amusing voice acting.
-Amy's gameplay is slow, but is quite fun. Although the HUB worlds clearly weren't made with Amy's speed in mind, the levels make up for it. You run away from one of Eggman's robots called Zero as he tries to steal the bird that you are protecting. Story is nothing special, gameplay is fine. 6/10
-Gamma is a very interesting character. He has an amazing story that really captures you and makes you want to see more of him. The story is very short, but the shoot 'em up style is a nice break and the story is great. The stages including a timer does not help the story's length and I feel that it is unnecessary. 8/10
-Big is an intersting character. Short story, lack of mechanics, funny voice, stages that can be completed in seconds. Big is filler... Quite literally. 3/10
Overall, this port is not good. There are way too many space-fillers and lazy design such as Sky Chase, the repeated bosses and levels and the whole of Big the Cat's story (even though Big was a promo character).
The camera will get stuck very often and the physics aren't good. The graphics are worse than the original Dreamcast version somehow.
I would recommend trying out the Dreamcast version over any other for this game. It is more visually appealing and it somehow works better than the later ports. The only downside is that you can't skip the cutscenes on Dreamcast.

What can I, a random Steam user, say about Sonic Adventure DX that hasn't already been said in the 18 years since its initial release on the Dreamcast? Not a whole lot, that's what. But con-sardit, Steam is letting me write a review, so I'm going to give it a try anyway!
This is Sonic's first real steps into 3D gaming if we can all permit ourselves to disregard that one other game that we shall all permit ourselves to disregard. And after 18 years, it's safe to say that ol' SADX didn't age quite as well as his little brother. But DX is still a fun game to play once you get past the blocky character models, awkward animations, and downright abysmal voice-acting. It's main draw is that it isn't just one game, but rather six different games tied together through a plot about Sonic and his friends (and one guy he's never met before and a robot that he almost killed) stopping Eggman (pardon me, Robotnik) from using an ancient evil water monster to conquer the world...or rather, one city. Or destroy the city so he can make his own. Ivo, things would be a lot simpler if you just ran for mayor. Just saying.
Each character has their own gameplay style. Sonic is the action platforming that we've all come to know and love. Tails is the exact same as Sonic, only he can completely break the game by flying around to beat Sonic to the end of the level, and make the level designer cry themself to sleep from having their hard work wasted by a mutant fox.
Knuckles is a platforming treasure hunter game which is honestly my favortie of the bunch. Sega could likely make an entire game out of treasure hunting, so long as they use the radar system of this game, and not that nonsense from SA2B. Sega, if you want us to play longer, just give us more to play with. Don't try to pass off a neutered radar as innovation.
Where was I? Right. Amy, in her first playable appearance is...it's hard to summarize it, really. You spend the levels running away from a big green can robot and bashing everything with a giant hammer. It's kinda like a stealth game where stealth is is either completely optional, or just not an option at all. You could try to hide, but it's ultimately more fun to just go about murdering everything in sight...oh wait, that's it. Amy's levels are Metal Gear Solid with a pink anime hedgehog.
E-102 Beta, a new character, plays by running around and shooting everything. I can't help but feel this is what Mega Man would play like if given a Z-axis.
The last new character is Big the Cat.
As I said, the plot revolves around Eggman using an ancient water monster to do evil, but only Sonic and Tails actually address this matter. The other four are more or less off doing their own thing, bumping into each other on occasion. Knuckles is trying to fix his Master Emerald, Amy is reuniting bird families, and Beta is going on a feels trip and dragging the player right along.
Big the Cat also does things.
Occasionally, a red Navi teleports a character to the distant past so the player can get a clue as to what is even going on. These flashbacks are solely for the players benefits. The characters never get any indication as to why they are in the past, and once they return, they just go on about their day without a second thought as to where they just were. It's as if they had been lost in a daydream, and nothing more.
You may be asking yourself why I'm not going into any detail about Big the Cat.
All in all, even though the game has aged like milk and the plot is a jumbled mess, I can't help but reccmmend this game Maybe it's nostalgia, or maybe there's something great to this game that I simply can't put into words, but it definitely deserves to be played at least once.

So I bet nobody expected this review from me but here we go. Sonic Adventure is surprisingly one of my favourite Sonic games may I say even as good if not way better than Adventure 2 and dare I say some of the 2D games aswell. This game was revolutionary for it's time (1998 in Japan) and here in the States when the Dreamcast launched in 1999. It may not have aged as well as some may like but for an "early 3D game" the graphics , sound , design and gameplay overall were completely fine. The transition from 2D to 3D may have not been as well received as some might've hoped but it really is hard to come off the success of Sonic 3 & Knuckles.
The models are really except the mouth movements are.....jarring to say the least. The music is overall nice especially the non lyrical songs but soem of those are catchy at least fitting even but a very "in it's time period" kind of thing. The story while pretty generic is interesting is some aspects and each of the 6 characters will have their slight alterations of the story and dialogue dependant on that specific character which adds a bit of flavor to it that Adventure 2 lacks and these 6 characters stories all intertwine at some point(s) too. Despite the human world setting alot of aspects of the game keep true and reference the classics for those of you who like that because sadly after this point I feel that Sonic lost it's way with that with trying to hard to fit into the new millennium and being "edgy".
Now each of the 6 characters have different gameplay styles not gonna lie Sonic's IS the best but I expect nothing less from the gameplay of the title character. Sonic runs and jumps like you all rememeber from the older games along with new abilities too. His levels are also the best too which is good as his story is obviously the longest but the most straightforward trying to find and keep the chaos emeralds from Eggman. Tails plays similar to Sonic but can fly and hover in short bursts with his own little set of new moves. Tails levels revolve around races or timers so think of it like Sonic stages on a timer but he can also visit specific parts of the stages that Sonic cannot so not much to complain here for Sonic and Tails gameplay.
Knuckles gameplay is basically finding pieces of the master emerald the locations are switched up each time you visit the stage but you are given a radar which keeps track of where the 3 pieces are in the stage. Unlike Sonic Adventure 2 you can use the radar to track each of the pieces all at once instead of one at a time. Some of Knuckles sections are vastly different due to the hunting nature of his gameplay along with his climbing ability he has from the games prior he also comes with his new abilities too. His gameplay is a nice change of pace from the other gameplay styles and doesn't bog down the game. Amy is a slower moving character who uses her unique hammer abilities to attack and jump to higher places. Her levels mainly focus on running away from a robot trying to capture her it's different from what we usually see in this series and while she isn't really important in the overall story besides Gamma's section really it's not a bad thing and I somewhat like her section the biggest downfall for her portion is I feel they could've done more with her "puzzle" sections or the sections where you gotta figure something out. Like more of the color cube sectinos or something alike it would've been nice.
Let's get the worst part out of the way and that is Big the Cat while being voiced by John St Jon is a plus he has no importance on the plot except a minor detail involving his friend froggy. His gameplay revolves around fishing which isn't a bad thing per-say but in a Sonic the Hedgehog game? No just no. Luckily his 4 stages can be completed in like a minute each so his portion is the shortest he gets a few abilities/upgrades too surprisingly but yeah there you go we got fishing in a Sonic game. Lastly we have E102 Gamma which plays out similarly to other characters as far as stage design goes he is a bit slower and uses his gun to shoot down enemies and obsticles in his path. Very interesting gamepaly even if you wouldn't expect it in a Sonic game it is pretty fun and he has the best story in the game honestly and really gets into detail and the perspective of one of the tiny animals trapped in a robot which animals being stuck in the enemies has always been a staple for this series so it was nice seeing how Gamma's story played out as he went around "saving" his friends. Then after you beat all of these characters stories you will unlock a secret I mean we all know what at this point but for the sake of this review i'll leave the final portion of this game a surprise. Did I forget to mention you can play each character at your own pace? That is alot better than the forced playstyle and narrative's on the sequel. It's also nice that this adventure actually feels like an adventure with hubs to explore and find stuff and fun little mini games here and there to play.
All in all the game may not have aged well in it's 15+ years of release and it may very well not be a "great" Sonic game or game in general but it's a game that while some small portions may be lackluster the overall experience is a fun ride and well worth checking out for one of the last good Sonic games (not counting handheld titles) even if the PC version has some glitches here and there.

The nostalgia brought by this game is incredible. I still have my Dreamcast here, even though it does not work anymore. But Sonic Adventure is a big part of my childhood and I'm glad to have the chance to finally beat Chaos now that I know a little bit more about how to play!

Like Tomb Raider: Anniversary this is one is kinda hard to recommend but I'm only doing so because I found enough enjoyment and challenge out of the game to do so.
Controls are FAR better than the old school Tomb Raider games and movement feels much quicker. The core game play is largely still the same however - risky platforming, a few puzzles, and the dual pistols. Combat was fairly worse in my opinion however and for a tomb raider game there is A LOT of it.
The core issues with the combat comes from a few factors:
(1) Only one extra weapon to use than pistols, which you pick up from humans. Just use assault rifle ALL THE TIME. SMG isn't as strong or accurate and the shotguns range is pathetically short its useless in most situations.
(2) 95% or so of the enemies are generic humans with guns. Running out of ammo for your secondary weapon is very uncommon and their AI is essentially to stand in one spot and shoot.
(3) Uninspired boss fights. They are mostly shoot and dodge until a brief window opens up to use some gimmick such as a turret, shooting a platform, or swinging a grappling hook at a clearly pointed out object. Most of them are not hard at all and were not that fun.
Graphically it isn't anything spectacular but for its age it's fairly solid. There are FAR less bugs than Anniversary but there is one pain in the butt bug you will run into a couple of times that is more or less guaranteed to happen and it will crash your game. Just a heads up to get around this: reload the game, go to settings, turn off the next gen graphics option, play past the part that crashes, then re-enable the setting.
So between the crash bug and the often repetitive combat why do I recommend it? Because I still found it interesting enough for a play through. HOWEVER one caveat to that - I generally enjoy tomb raider games. Always did growing up and for the most part still do. If you're not a tomb raider fan and you are not planning on playing the sequel to this (Tomb Raider: Underworld), chances are you won't want to get this unless its on sale for cheap.

So, as you can see, I've played a fair bit of this game. Anyone who is into simulators and trucks can see why.
I like to take games like these serious, as if I was actually behind the wheel of that beast of a truck, hauling that heavy trailer with important cargo on it that just HAS to arrive in time, while also making sure to keep to the speed limits and not hit anything or anyone!
Here are the basic rules:
Yes, yes. I know, I know. But it's a simulator, right? It's meant to simulate, as best as possible, what it's like to do this for real? Well, I like to really immerse myself in these types of games. So, of course I'm going to worry about causing an accident! I don't want to ruin people's days, or♥♥♥♥♥♥off the client. Or spend half that money I just made from this job to repair my truck because I was too careless!
Well no, not quite. It's not really too expensive. Even less so when you get more experienced, level up your skills and therefore earn more money for a job, considering you're a more valuable driver. However, the prices can get high if you're stupid enough to race at around 90 mph down the motorway, and think you can take the turn-off at around 70-80. At that point, you're likely to crash into the barriers several times, and maybe even flip your truck. Even if you're lucky enough to not flip, your engine will malfunction. You'll be cruising along, at a cosy 60 mph, all of a sudden your engine shuts down, an error message pops up on your dash and your truck basically does an emergency stop.
. So, after a crash that caused quite a bit of damage, you can choose to risk your engine constantly going off, or you can call a tow truck that will take you to the nearest town/city. Obviously that will cost you, both money and time! So do be careful when you drive  around, especially with an urgent and important delivery!
Having said all that, sometimes it's kinda fun to just mess around. Who doesn't like to find out what it's like to drive through town at 70 mph?! If you have enough cash, and are willing to waste some, go right ahead and see just how fast that new truck you just bought can really go!
Of course, you can also upgrade and customize your truck. There are Service Stations in every city (that I'm aware of). There, you can make repairs to your truck, like replacing your tires that are starting to wear out. Go to a Service Station, select "Service" and a list will come up on the right side. It will list all the parts of your truck, what their damage is, and what it costs to repair it. All of the parts are automatically selected for repair, however you can pick and choose what you want to repair. Just note, whenever something has suffered too much damage, it will cause you problems. Just like in the real world! If your tires wear out too much, it will be more difficult to control your truck, since you won't have the traction that shiny new tires do. If you don't repair your engine, it will malfunction at random times and shut down. That can be several times in 1 minute, or happen once every 10 minutes. I'm not sure what will happen with the other parts, but I can guess that it's not going to make for a very comfortable and enjoyable drive...
To upgrade and customize your truck, go to a Service Station, and select Upgrade Shop. This will bring you to another screen where you can select a new Cab, Chassis, Engine, Transmission, Left or Right Steering Wheel, Paint, Outside Accessories and Inside Accessories. When you select either of the Accessories, some gray dots will appear on certain parts of your truck. Clicking on one will display parts on the list to the left. Hovering over a part will show you what it will look like on your truck. Clicking on it will install it.
Once you're finished, confirm your order at the bottom of the list and all the changes you've made will be saved. If, however you want to remove something from your order, just click on "See Changes", and select the part/s you want to remove, or just clear your order.
Once you've confirmed your order, you can leave the menu and see that beautiful new truck you've just spent the last hour creating! Why not take a screenshot and share it?
Another thing you can do is connect your profile to World of Trucks. You will have the option to sign into your account, or make a new one in-game. Once you've done that, you can go to the World of Trucks website. There you can set up your profile, see your truck stats for both ETS2 and ATS, as long as they are both connected to your account. You will also be able to change your licence plate number, for both games. Choose which Country/State the plate is from, then enter whatever you like. If you take pictures of your truck in-game through the Picture Mode, you will be able to see them in the Picture Manager in-game. There you can select which pictures to upload to your WoT account, and which one you'd like to set as a profile picture (the picture for that game, where you will see the truck stats). Whenever you upload a picture, anyone will be able to see it. Logged in users will also be able to like, favourite and comment on your picture, so remember to keep your pants on and smile before you take a selfie!
Once you've explored the game enough, you have your company set up, several garages and people working for you, bringing in so much cash you can basically move to Hawaii and retire. Or you've just got the hang of the controls of the game, but you don't like the idea of playing this awesome game all by yourself, then you can try and find a multiplayer mod for this. Personally, I use TruckersMP. You can use it with both American Truck Simulator, and Euro Truck Simulator 2. It uses your save game, so you will have everything you do in the single player version, but in multiplayer!
Of course you can also use mods through the Steam Workshop. Personally, I use mods that remove traffic, and I also got a mod that gives me a lot of XP. That way I will have all the parts unlocked in the Upgrade Shop and spend the next 2 hours going through all the new parts and paint jobs, and then try to make a truck that I'm proud to drive around the EU.
Just note that TruckersMP has some rules around mods, so any mods that are through the Steam Workshop will be disabled when launching the game with TruckersMP!

There’s a lot to love about Alone With You. You play as the lone survivor in a doomed terraforming colony, you’re only hope of escape is fixing up an escape ship before the planet’s tumultuous weather destroys everything around you. Unfortunately, both you and your AI companion lack the knowledge to perform such a repair. Fortunately, your AI companion has a data store which contains the memories and personalities of 4 colonists who were all indirectly working on solutions to your very problem. As you meet all 4 characters – through holographic recreations – you’ll learn more about the characters as they help you to escape. In a smart twist however – the memories of these individuals aren’t quite up to date, ending as the rift incident happened, giving you a chance to deliver closure to each.
Whilst survival is your driving instinct, the real meat of the game is in it’s stories. As you explore the various levels, you’ll come across environmental cues, notes, and tidbits of information that help you to form a rounded description of what happened. The relationships and personalities – not only of the four holograms – are exposed in this fashion and for a narrative-fanatic like me, it helps to provide what is a fantastic atmosphere, putting me in the mind of such classics as ‘Beneath a Steel Sky’, ‘Another World’, and ‘2001: A Space Odyssey’.
It’s while mentioning ‘Beneath a Steel Sky’ however that my biggest criticism of Alone With You rears it’s ugly head. With all of those retro point ‘n click vibes, I was left unsatisfied by the puzzles I found myself solving. ‘Puzzles’ is probably a little bit strong – there is nothing in Alone With You that causes more than a brief second of pause. Like ‘puzzles’, ‘solving’ is also too strong a word for it. As you explore each level, you cannot fail to stumble upon answers. Another disappointing aspect was that the answers to certain puzzles fail to contain any logic – in one level which immediately springs to mind, you have to figure out the passcode for a door. Coincidentally, the password is made up of numbers you find in unrelated texts – texts which have no link nor reasoning as to why they’d be used as the passcode.
In a later level however, Alone With You perfectly executes the same setup – you have to figure out a passcode but this time you’re given a clue. To solve it you must read various texts and environmental clues to put the answer together yourself. Having to reach for paper and pen, and actually put these facts together delighted my simple mind. The feeling that more of the same spread throughout the game would have elevated Alone With You a couple of levels, is not one that I can shake.
For most, Alone With You will last for around 6 – 7 hours but there is some replayability to be had. The Steam release features a number of achievements, several of which revolve around the conversations you have with the four holograms. In my play-through, I made an early decision to stick to Winnie like glue, earning myself an achievement for doing so. For achievement hunters, a second play-through is needed to also spend each ‘special’ meeting with a different hologram. Several endings are also available in the game and as things come to a head, a decision you must make. That decision dramatically alters how your story ends.
What impressed me most about Alone With You was it’s ability to make me think about myself – it sounds cliche, I know – but I found myself projecting my personality onto the protagonist, thoughts that took me by surprise popped up as a I questioned how I wanted to approach conversations and specifically the ending. Your final choice is one which has logical outcomes completely dependent on the type of person that you are, and that’s kind of neat.
Alone With You is an interactive story well worth your time, uninspired puzzles let down the point 'n click vibe but a strong narrative is told extremely well through conversing with holographic simulations and by finding notes, datapads, and recordings in well designed environments. The soundtrack is fitting and helps to create a hard sci-fi atmosphere.

Alone with you is a sci-fi point and click adventure game which deals with you as the last survivor who luckily survives a disaster which killed every one of his crew members. With the help of an AI partner, you are tasked to find out how are you going to escape out of this settlement.
The “you” in Alone with you is the computer partner who also generates various holograms of the crew members who died in the disaster by calculating the data stored in the settlement which leads you to solve the mystery and escape. It plays exactly like how you would expect a classic point and click adventure plays like. You walk around the desolate station collecting various things, finding out bits of lore about the story and solve puzzles to progress further in the story.
These puzzles are not exactly difficult but require you to pay attention to your surroundings and the dialogues. There were a few times where the answer to a particular puzzle was given away in a previous dialogue and I had failed to realize that which lead to two hours of frustration.
Interactive games like these depend on a good quality of storytelling which can keep you invested throughout the journey and Alone with you succeeds here with flying colours. Telling much about the story in the review will not do it justice and you have to experience it yourself to see the various routes it takes and how emotional it gets towards the end. There are two endings to the game and they both are different enough to warrant some replayabilty. The dialogues are also a little different based on items you pick up through the journey and all of them are written very well.
While the story is really great, there is some stretched out sections in the middle section of the story. These involve you going back and forth to the same parts of the settlement without much progression in the story. These sections felt padded out and felt like the developers had to cram in these parts just to increase the length of the game. While this was a souring experience, it is completely overshadowed by the great way the story is told in the game. The characters are all very well developed and you grow a connection with them towards the end.
Alone with you’s pixelated art design helps it a lot. The environments themselves tell the story of the desolate settlement and even though there is no blood and gore, there were some rooms which feel gut wrenching when you walk into them.
The settlement with no other interaction other than you AI companion and the hologram representation of the mechanics makes you feel like you are abandoned in a place you don’t want to be and yet towards the end, these creepy settlements grow to be your home. These visuals carry the game to a whole another level and while not hyper realistic, they do their job spectacularly.
Another field in which Alone with you excels in is its sound design. The soundtrack is brilliant with a sci-fi touch and adds to the desolate feeling. There is no voice acting to speak of and I think the game is better without it as it might have ruined the experience.
If you like Point and click adventure games then Alone with you would not disappoint you. It tells a great emotional story and is gut wrenching in parts. If you don’t like games like this where there is little actual gameplay then Alone with you won’t do anything to change your mind. But at this price, I think that you should give Alone with you a try, it might not be revolutionary but it is a solid experience nonetheless.

Alone With You developed by Benjamin Rivers Inc. is a sci-fi romance adventure game that definitely plays the part. (In this game, pixel graphics set the art style along with incorporating this title in the indie genre.)
Classic pixelated graphics aside, this space adventure aims on telling a deeper story and explore the introspective qualities of people ins space and maybe more simply—human beings in general. The story follow the only living survivor of a terraforming mission consisting of two colonies on a distant planet that have been destroyed by a deteriorating planet and unstable seismic activity.
Although Alone With You offered quite the interesting dialogue between holograms and the AI, I found that much of the time the gameplay accompanying the story was too much of a grind. The main premise being that you have three weeks to prepare by gathering supplies such as food, medicine, fuel and spare parts to repair your ship before you perish from exposure. I found that the game’s way of sending you on missions got very repetitive and boring. Despite that exploring the different facilities can be interesting, such as uncovering the clues to open a new area or finding the passage you’ve been looking for that was secretly hidden in an environment puzzle. Some of the ways the game hints to clues can be really sneaky and testing out what works can have its rewards. Overall, the fact that the gameplay had no deeper dimension throughout the mid-game really made the game feel more of a chore than engaging. I felt that at times I was just running through a mission just to get closer to the end to see how it all played out.

Oh, how I love this game. It got me into the Tomb Raider series way back when it was released in 2006. I'd dabbled in the older entries on the PlayStation but could never beat them (until recently that is. Check out my reviews for them! No shameful self-promotion here!), but Legend piqued my interest in the series and alas, $20 later, I have the entire series on Steam. And what a brilliant way to start again. Tomb Raider: Legend is precisely what Lara Croft needed: a beautiful, seamless and user-friendly transition to the (then) next generation of gaming.
The majority of Tomb Raider's lore is retconned, but the essentials are all here. We still (of course) have Lara Croft, and man, has she recieved a facelift. And a boob job. And a butt job. I'm gay and even I can't stop staring at her. She's still the kickass, no-nonsense, incredibly acrobatic, academic and elegant explorer who we've come to know and love. And the same applies to the gameplay; you still raid tombs, you still discover hidden treasures while globetrotting, and shoot the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of bad guys and angry cats. All in a beautiful new engine.
Man, this game is pretty. It just looks phenomenal. It has a unique, semi-cartoonish style in terms of character models, but the environments are bursting with detail and realism, and the use of effects like bloom and motion blurs are used just enough not to take away from the experience. Textures are crisp, ragdolls are hilariously bouncy, animations are smoother than jelly, and the detail is immaculate. The first time Lara emerged from water, actually visably wet and her clothes drenched, I was in awe.
It sounds amazing, too. The effort that went into the soundtrack is very admirable. Troels Brun Folmann has crafted a dynamic, unique to each level musical score which only adds to the already excellent atmosphere. Voice acting is also great, a tad unbelievable but very cinematic. Keeley Hawes brings a regal and more mature tone to Lara which I was very glad to hear.
Plot-wise, it's good! I mean, nothing really new or special here. It's the typical "artifact in multiple pieces go around the world to collect them and then something happens when they're all together then boss battle". But there are some lovely villains, there's traitors, there's emotion, there's consistency, and there's enough to keep you interested in what's going on. I don't think as much effort was put in here as in The Angel of Darkness, but it works and it wraps up nicely, hinting at a sequel without resorting to an irritating cliffhanger. That said, the research that Crystal Dynamics did into ancient lore, such as that of King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table, do give the story a lot more depth.
The gameplay itself? Stellar. It feels so incredibly natural when Lara is rope-swinging, vaulting, shimmying, dodging, shooting, pole-climbing, swimming, and even riding a Ducati™ (yes, there's product placement) motorcycle. The levels are incredibly varied, and I don't miss the older blocky engine one iota. Movement and combat is far less restrictive, control is pitch-perfect, and the addition of Lara's grappling hook adds a lot more than one would think to the game. It's very smooth and well done. There's also tons of unlockables, which I absolutely LOVE. What happened to unlockables?! There's (many) costumes, weapon upgrades, art, models, cheats and a video to unlock, and all this encourages replayability.
Which brings me to the few negative points I have about this game. My main gripe is the length: there are only eight levels in Tomb Raider: Legend (nine, if you count Lara's Mansion, which makes a welcome return), and even with the added collectibles and time trials for each level, the game is over quickly, especially for people who don't care about 100% completion. The fact that it's quite easy (regardless of the difficulty setting) also adds to this; the game is constantly providing you with tutorials, even in the sixth level of the game, and you can utilise Lara's magical binoculars to help you solve puzzles (none of which are remotely complex).
The game is also buggy from time to time, mostly in the visual department. I noticed this especially in Kazakhstan, during a motorcycle section in which areas of the map were simply missing or transparent. Turning on "Next-Generation Content" in the video settings adds dynamic lighting and better textures, but kills the framerate (sometimes regardless of your gaming setup) and throws even more glitches into the mix, including misaligned ropes and distorted faces, and even crashing the game on some levels.
One final thing: Lara's new sidekicks bug me, a lot. They just don't shut the hell up. "Watch out Lara!" "Wow Lara, that was great!" "Whoa, I don't like the look of this!". Even Lara herself gets audibly annoyed with them. It's totally nitpicking on my part but I feel it's a valid criticism. Just shut the hell up Zip and Alister! She doesn't need your help!
Do I recommend this game? Absolutely. Legend was the start of something new, a rebirth that Tomb Raider so desperately needed. After Legend came onto the scene, the equally awesome Anniversary, Underworld, Guardian of Light and the 2013 re-imagining followed suit. What an excellent way to get us exploring again!

At the tender age of 9 years old, Lara Croft and her mother Amelia, survive a plane crash in the Himalayan mountains. Taking refuge in an old monastery, young Lara, already with an adventurous heart, discovers a stone dais with an ancient sword in it. This triggers an event that leads to her mother disappearance, and is the premise to Tomb Raider Legend.
This was the first Tomb Raider developed by Crystal Dynamics, Eidos Interactive switched the development of the next Tomb Raider game away from Core Design (the studio was shut down a little while after this decision) after the poorly received Angel of Darkness failed in the eyes of most Tomb Raider fans, and professional critics.
Tomb Raider Legend was/is an excellent Tomb Raider game, with the perfect balance between puzzle solving and combat, and an intricate story that mixes myth and marries it with real exotic locations to explore.
Graphics wise, this is a game from 2006, but it holds very well to this day. The textures are well detailed and the particle system and animations are particularly impressive. The music in the game is on par with other Tomb Raider titles, which means that it's very good as well. Orchestrated music that kicks in at the right time to give an extra dose of suspense never gets old, and it's classic Tomb Raider in that regard.
New mechanics were also introduced this time around. Lara now has the ability to slow down time versus human enemies, but you can only use it when at a real close range by double pressing the jump button. When it's active time slows down and your aiming is more precise and you can target and damage more than one enemy if you are fast enough. A flashlight was also introduced and you can manually turn it on or off, and it is essencial in dark areas. You can carry only 3 medkits at any given time, and you can choose to use them whenever the situation calls for it. The amount of weapons you can carry is limited to only 2, your dual pistols and an extra slot for whichever weapon you want to carry. For the first time in a Tomb Raider game, you can pick up weapons from your fallen enemies, and there is some variation to them, from a shotgun, to an SMG, a rifle and a grenade launcher, plus a surprise weapon close to the end of the game. Another franchise first is the abbility to carry grenades. The binoculars are also very important, specially for helping you out with puzzle solving, with the ability to enter RAD mode and identify movable objects, destructable structures and mechanisms.
The characters and voice acting in the game are top notch. The script is well written and very well executed by the voice actors. They do a great job with emotions, the way the lines are delivered and acted make you feel in empathy with the characters, either it's a dramatic moment, or a cheerful one. Lara is not alone in this adventure, as her companions Zip and Allister always provide insight and advice through her intercom. These characters are not particularly deep, but they serve their purpose well and without getting in the way. Lara however is not the only true "deep" character in the game, as some characters have real motivations as well (can't really say much more without spoiling it to anyone) that make perfect sense in terms of story.
The puzzles in the game are logical and challenging for the most part, without ever becoming frustrating. The combat is fun, but the controls are a little clunky, and the enemy A.I apart from boss fights is just way too easy and not all that great. There is some texture distortion on this particular PC version, but it is rare and does not detract from the experience. I have read that some people have had some issues with this game under modern Operating Systems, but having played the game on Windows 7 Ultimate 64 bit, I never encountered any issues or crashes of any sort. It runs like a charm on my OS. Also worthy of mention, and in my opinion a negative aspect of this version is the lack of the Steam overlay, meaning you will not be able to shift+tab to access the steam community while playing, your only option is to alt+tab, and doing so never caused the game to crash for me. There is a workaround to this issue, so I am told, but I did not try it out, and therefore can't really say anything on that aspect.
Tomb Raider Legend is an amazing Tomb Raider game. While not perfect, it is well worth playing.
For it's current price, it's a steal (even more so when it goes on sale, it can go as low as 1,50$) and well worth it. The game is a little short compared to other Raider games, but it is a fun and thrilling ride from start to finish.
8/10
The Good
Graphics still hold out well today
Lifelike animation, truly great music and sound effects
Voice acting and story are top notch
Some extra stuff to unlock which adds replayability
Good selection of guns, fun and logical puzzles, exotic and mystical locations to explore
Challenging Boss fights
Motorcycle sections are fun
The Bad
Some texture distortion
Combat is a little clunky
Enemy A.I is not very smart
No Steam overlay without a fix
